summary: Grand strategy — the hierarchical subordination of means to ends across time and domain — has become structurally impossible in the contemporary United States and European Union. This is not a claim about leadership, ideology, or democratic dysfunction. It is a claim about slack: the degrees of freedom available to a system for purposive reconfiguration. Cross-sector coupling, whose monotonic increase since 1945 is established in The Tragedy of the Citadel, has consumed that slack. As coupling rises, every sector becomes a veto point, every adjustment reverberates across the whole, and the system's only remaining imperative is equilibrium maintenance. What replaces strategy is adjustment: the continuous, headless, path-dependent metabolisation of crises into further coupling.   The paper is a continuation of the Citadel monograph. What it contributes is fourfold. First, the concept of strategic slack, with the formal apparatus that distinguishes it from complexity and from prosperity. Second, the three mechanisms by which coupling crowds out strategy: veto proliferation, adjustment costs, and temporal compression. Third, the kinesis/praxis distinction: the headless configuration exhibits behaviour without action, motion without agency. Fourth, the category of the headless ruling structure — a class in itself but not for itself, defined by structural position in the coupling network rather than by collective consciousness, coordinated through coupling rather than through deliberation. The category is distinguished from six adjacent literatures and integrated with the Citadel Class: the Citadel is the extraction face of the structural elite; the headless ruling structure is its governance face.   The argument bears on Ukraine, Iran, and industrial policy, and it extends the phase transition analysis the Citadel established. The headless configuration does not merely fail to satisfy the four conditions for durable decoupling. It actively prevents their satisfaction, because each condition requires an agent whose existence the configuration has eliminated. The paper raises three questions it does not answer — whether headless configurations recur, whether the modern state was an exception or a baseline, and whether the class conflict that produced the couplings has ended or merely changed form — and specifies what would be required to settle them.
title: The Headless Citadel: Governance Without a Chooser

summary: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) swarms increasingly rely on language-model agents to provide adaptive mission-level reasoning in uncertain environments. Fully distributed control, in which each UAV hosts an independent Small Language Model (SLM), removes reliance on a centralized coordinator but introduces an information-management problem: long-running interaction histories can degrade the reasoning context, while indiscriminate information dissemination increases communication and inference overhead. We address these challenges with a distributed UAV-agent architecture that enables continuous local SLM control through an event-driven reason-act-observe lifecycle. Runtime knowledge is represented as structured atomic notes and organized into core, local, and peer-specific memory. A deterministic interest-aware gossip engine selectively disseminates these notes according to recipient-specific semantic novelty and recency. We evaluate the architecture using ten UAVs in a simulated search-and-rescue mission. Our approach completes all experimental runs, whereas unrestricted flooding messages completes only 70-85\%, and delegating forwarding decisions to the SLM prevents mission completion in every run. Compared with unrestricted flooding, our approach approximately halves inference-token consumption, reduces transmitted data, and achieves lower survivor-count error.
title: Managing Context and Communication in Distributed Agentic UAV Swarms

summary: Multi-agent AI scientists have shown improving performance across a diverse range of tasks. Yet a common approach is design-time agentic orchestration, which typically relies on fixed workflows. In contrast, human scientists coordinate and adjust their division of labor at runtime. We therefore ask: can AI scientists also coordinate at runtime? To this end, we introduce Runtime Agent Coordination (RAC), which selects agents from existing AI-scientist hosts during execution, assigns scoped work contracts, and provides artifact-grounded verification. Verification informs subsequent agents without blocking transitions or discarding artifacts. We conduct a single-seed exploratory evaluation across Agent Laboratory, EvoScientist, and ARK on ResearchClawBench, preserving host models, tools, and permissions under host-calibrated budgets. Four cumulative conditions separate native execution, runtime communication, runtime selection, and the combined addition of contracts and verification. Runtime selection yields the highest observed mean score for each host; adding contracts and verification reduces these means, with host-dependent outcomes relative to native execution. These results motivate runtime coordination while exposing the limits of additional coordination mechanisms under constrained budgets. Code is available at https://github.com/systemind-team/Runtime-AI-Scientist.
title: Can AI Scientists Coordinate at Runtime?

summary: We present a complete, self-contained analysis of the one-loop functional renormalization group (FRG) flow of Quantum Distortion Gravity (QDG), a metric-affine framework with gauged Weyl symmetry. We derive the classical foundations from first principles: the irreducible decomposition of the distortion tensor with an explicit inversion of the trace matrix, the Weyl-covariant distortion $\tilde D$, the no-go theorem for bare distortion invariants, and the Weyl-invariant ultraviolet action with distortion entering through $\phi^2 I_i[\tilde D]$. We then establish the constraint structure of the truncated theory (8 physical degrees of freedom, no spin-2 ghost) via a complete Dirac--Bergmann analysis, and analyze the BRST--BV quantization of the gauge algebra $Diff(\mathcal M) \ltimes Weyl$, including the antifield spectrum, the nilpotency proof, and the classical master equation. We compute the Weyl anomaly coefficients from heat-kernel data and prove the anomaly is cancellable by a Wess--Zumino term. In the main part of the paper we derive all one-loop beta functions from first principles, keeping every intermediate step. We show that in unitary gauge, the dilaton is a gauge mode and does not contribute; Proca fields contribute with three transverse polarizations and no Faddeev--Popov ghosts; Dirac fermions contribute via the Litim fermionic regulator. We extract the matter coefficients $a_S = +1/2$, $a_D = -2$, and $a_V = +3/2$ (the last for a Proca vector in unitary gauge), and we verify each by two independent routes. We derive the gravitational anomalous dimension from the explicit trace over TT graviton, trace mode, and Faddeev--Popov ghosts, reproducing the Litim result $A(\lambda)$ and $B(\lambda)$, and we display the ADM decomposition that yields the mode multiplicities. We show that the fixed-point equation $\beta_{\tilde G} = 0$ is genuinely quadratic in $\tilde G$ at fixed $\lambda$, we solve it explicitly, and we give the resulting discriminant. For the Standard Model matter content ($n_f = 3$, $n_V = 2$), we find a non-trivial UV fixed point at $\tilde G^* \approx 0.43$, $\lambda^* \approx -0.02$, with two relevant directions in the $(\tilde G, \lambda)$ sector, and we compute the stability matrix, critical exponents, and their numerical uncertainties. We verify robustness with a sensitivity scan, showing the fixed point exists for all $C_{\rm bl} > C_{\rm bl}^{\rm crit} \approx -1.02$, well above the QDG value $C_{\rm bl} = -3/(2\pi) \approx -0.477$; we give the analytic form of the critical line. We also analyze the heat kernel in a background field strength $F_{\mu\nu}$, showing that the mixing between graviton and Proca in the $(h^{01}, V^1)$ sector gives a negative contribution to the FRG coefficient $\hat c_V$ (distinct from the Weyl-anomaly coefficient $c^{\rm W}$), and we exhibit the second-order heat-kernel trace explicitly. Finally, we discuss scale generation via Coleman--Weinberg in a two-scalar extension, derive the flat-direction condition, and compare our results with the recent Proca--gravity fixed point of Pastor-Marcos et al. All symbolic and numerical calculations are performed in Python (SymPy, NumPy, SciPy), and the complete code is provided in the appendices, together with additional verification scripts.
title: Quantum Distortion Gravity: A Complete One-Loop Analysis of the Minimal Truncation

summary: Grand strategy — the hierarchical subordination of means to ends across time and domain — has become structurally impossible in the contemporary United States and European Union. This is not a claim about leadership, ideology, or democratic dysfunction. It is a claim about slack: the degrees of freedom available to a system for purposive reconfiguration. Cross-sector coupling, whose monotonic increase since 1945 is established in The Tragedy of the Citadel, has consumed that slack. As coupling rises, every sector becomes a veto point, every adjustment reverberates across the whole, and the system's only remaining imperative is equilibrium maintenance. What replaces strategy is adjustment: the continuous, headless, path-dependent metabolisation of crises into further coupling.   The paper is a continuation of the Citadel monograph. What it contributes is fourfold. First, the concept of strategic slack, with the formal apparatus that distinguishes it from complexity and from prosperity. Second, the three mechanisms by which coupling crowds out strategy: veto proliferation, adjustment costs, and temporal compression. Third, the kinesis/praxis distinction: the headless configuration exhibits behaviour without action, motion without agency. Fourth, the category of the headless ruling structure — a class in itself but not for itself, defined by structural position in the coupling network rather than by collective consciousness, coordinated through coupling rather than through deliberation. The category is distinguished from six adjacent literatures and integrated with the Citadel Class: the Citadel is the extraction face of the structural elite; the headless ruling structure is its governance face.   The argument bears on Ukraine, Iran, and industrial policy, and it extends the phase transition analysis the Citadel established. The headless configuration does not merely fail to satisfy the four conditions for durable decoupling. It actively prevents their satisfaction, because each condition requires an agent whose existence the configuration has eliminated. The paper raises three questions it does not answer — whether headless configurations recur, whether the modern state was an exception or a baseline, and whether the class conflict that produced the couplings has ended or merely changed form — and specifies what would be required to settle them.
title: The Headless Citadel: Governance Without a Chooser

summary: This record contains the replication package accompanying the article “DCMT-Cert: Empirical Adequacy Certification of Machine-Learning Data-Contract Gates.” The package provides the scripts, retained numerical outputs, analysis tables, audit materials, dataset manifests, source hashes, and checksum information required to reproduce and inspect the computational analyses reported in the article. The materials cover the paired clean-versus-clean harm calibration, the Stage 1 policy-development analysis, the Stage 2 confirmation analysis, all five prespecified operating profiles, policy selection and multiplicity analyses, baseline comparisons, broadened fault analyses, model-family validation, native Great Expectations validation, harm-threshold sensitivity, provenance and transfer audits, and supporting consistency checks. The package is organised using descriptive file names and is intended to permit independent inspection and reproduction of the reported computational results. The accompanying article defines the experimental protocol, scope of the empirical certificates, statistical interpretation, and limitations of the study.
title: Replication Package for "DCMT-Cert: Empirical Adequacy Certification of Machine-Learning Data-Contract Gates"

summary: The Visibility Problem Hypershape Shadow Hypothesis II   Chloe J. Tully https://orcid.org/0009-0007-5661-7332 HSH Paper 1 https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23010822 Project UAP Studies   v0.1 3 October 2026 Preprint. Not peer-reviewed.   Companion to HSH I (28 September 2026). Tier-2 material is not in this paper.     DISCIPLINE   HSH I derived a geometry and assumed a flux law. This paper keeps the geometry and splits the assumption. What is proved is proved about the toy model. What is not selected — a coupling, a bulk metric, a relativistic completion — is named and left open. Neural coupling and retrocausality are still excluded. They are not implied by anything below.     ABSTRACT   HSH I predicted a parabolic light curve by taking received flux proportional to the area of the brane slice. That step is not geometry. For a 4-ball translating along the hidden axis, orthographic area scales as ρ² and reproduces the parabola F₂ = 1 − (t/τ)². Uniform emission through the 3-volume of the same slice scales as ρ³ and produces F₃ = [1 − (t/τ)²]^(3/2). The families meet at onset, peak, and end, and disagree in the shoulders: at |t/τ| = 1/√2, F₂ = 1/2 while F₃ = 1/(2√2). Calibrated photometry can tell them apart.   A 4-ellipsoid at fixed orientation in the XW plane stays inside both families, for every line of sight. An orientation that changes during the transit need not. One computed counterexample is given. The C₅ cover twist proposed in open problem O5 — cross-edges (i, 0) ↔ (i+1, 1) in place of the self-steps — is isomorphic to the untwisted cover, so the 1/φ gap is unchanged. No uniform self-step weight puts the even sector on the five-value spectrum flagged in HSH I. Coupling remains the critical open problem. Ansätze are stated with kill criteria. None is adopted.     CONTENTS   1. What HSH I already fixed 2. Two measures, two light curves 3. Fixed orientation stays parabolic 4. The C₅ twist does not close O5 5. Coupling ansätze, none chosen 6. What this does not unlock 7. Status of claims

summary: Mathematics, as taught in schools, has historically been presented as a universal, neutral, and decontextualized body of knowledge, contributing to the maintenance of exclusionary and Eurocentric curricular practices. This conception ignores the plurality of ways of producing, organizing, and using mathematical knowledge in different cultural groups, generating processes of alienation and school failure, especially among students whose experiences do not align with the hegemonic mathematical culture. This article discusses Ethnomathematics as a theoretical-methodological perspective and research program, an indispensable epistemological and formative field in the initial training of mathematics teachers. The objective is to analyze how Ethnomathematics can be integrated into the undergraduate mathematics curriculum, to enable future teachers to recognize, value, and articulate mathematical knowledge from different cultural groups with academic mathematics, promoting an inclusive, critical, and socially committed education. To this end, it is based on several theoretical frameworks that encompass Ethnomathematics, teacher training, and critical pedagogical approaches, such as those of Freire and Skovsmose. After investigations, readings, and rereading, it is concluded that the systematic integration of Ethnomathematics into initial teacher training contributes to the decolonization of the curriculum, the humanization of mathematics teaching, and the training of reflective teachers committed to social justice.
title: ETHNOMATHEMATICS AS A THEORETICAL AND METHODOLOGICAL PERSPECTIVE IN THE INITIAL TRAINING OF MATHEMATICS TEACHERS

summary: This release updates the construction and documentation of the US industry-level production accounts for 1947–2023. Main updates Uses BEA–BLS nominal values from 1997 onward. Links pre-1997 US KLEMS capital, labor, and intermediate inputs to their 1997 BEA–BLS levels using industry- and component-specific ratios. Stabilizes industry identifiers across software versions. Adds cross-platform notebook execution for Windows, macOS, and Linux. Updates the README, notebook documentation, and methodological manual. Corrects variable descriptions in the intermediate workbook. Regenerates and validates all output datasets. The release provides results for 44 industries from 1947 to 2023 and 63 industries from 1963 to 2023. The complete replication pipeline has been successfully executed and validated.

summary: Data and code to reproduce all estimates and data figures in Onodje and Adekoya, "Imported climate inflation: Supplier weather shocks, trade networks and food prices in 154 economies". The package contains the country-month analysis panel for 154 economies (2000–2025) with its codebook, supporting processed files (supplier growing-season weather shocks, food balances, bilateral staple trade and foreign climate exposure measures), Python scripts that build the panel from public sources and produce all results, and the published figures. See README.md for the run order and data sources. CPI-based variables are derived from the IMF Consumer Price Index dataset and, for some economies, the FAOSTAT Consumer Price Indices. Source: International Monetary Fund; FAO. The data have been transformed by the authors (source selection by economy, Code is released under the MIT licence and data and figures under CC BY 4.0.

summary: Replication package for a study of whether synthetic stress tests are valid evidence of the forgetting (old-task regression) of deep object detectors fine-tuned to a new operating condition. It contains the protocol document with its dated change log (Turkish original and English translation, Annexes C–K), all training and analysis scripts (YOLOv8, YOLO11n, Faster R-CNN), the run logs with one row per adaptation, all analysis outputs, cached embeddings, and the generator that reproduces every number, table and figure of the manuscript. Images are not redistributed; dataset sources are listed in the README. Changes in 4.1: the embedding is made independent of batch composition (the training library letterboxes a batch to a rectangle when all its images share one size and to a square otherwise). Three field arms and the Annex J split were re-embedded and every analysis re-run; no validity verdict changed. Annex K (qualification at a different distance on RID and DAWN) is added. Version 4.0 was produced before this correction; both are retained, and the pre-correction files are also included in this version (folder old_batchdep_2eki) so the difference can be inspected. Earlier versions of this record hold the deposit of an earlier analysis under a different protocol; they are retained so the difference can be inspected.
title: Replication package for "Are Synthetic Stress Tests Valid Evidence of Forgetting? A Matched-Distance Validity Check for Adapted Deep Object Detectors"

summary: Analysis-ready aggregate data for a systematic review and meta-analysis comparing decompressive craniectomy more than 48 hours versus within 48 hours after onset in malignant middle cerebral artery infarction. Version 3 contains data and provenance records only. Contents: two-by-two counts for mortality (14 studies) and unfavorable functional outcome (12 studies) with exposure stratum, analysis role, outcome horizon and derivation; a cell-level provenance file giving, for every analyzed count, the extraction-workbook cell(s), their verbatim content and the arithmetic applied; arm-level counts by timing midpoint; and dual ROBINS-I ratings. Primary analysis (onset-to-surgery MCA cohorts; REML random effects with the modified Hartung-Knapp adjustment): mortality OR 1.136 (95% CI 0.705-1.832; k = 12; N = 585); unfavorable function OR 1.370 (0.812-2.313; k = 10; N = 511). Including the admission-timed administrative cohort and the mixed-territory cohort: 1.025 (0.800-1.314; k = 14) and 1.133 (0.896-1.434; k = 12). Changes from version 2: primary analysis restricted to onset-timed MCA cohorts; Shen 2024 mortality added; cell-level provenance added; figures and scripts removed.
title: Timing of decompressive craniectomy in malignant middle cerebral artery infarction: analysis-ready dataset and cell-level provenance for a systematic review and meta-analysis of surgery beyond 48 hours

summary: Scroll Score for Shift/Work ISSOTL17 Poster Presentation, Calgary, Canada Shift/Workshops are composed and disseminated by being performed. Playing the score leads to it being re-calibrated for future performances. Speculations was commissioned by the Kochi-Muziris Biennale, India. It was first performed at Edinburgh Sculpture Workshop (3-4 March 2017). At ESW, three ‘branch’ scores were composed to be performed in Kochi (22-23 March 2017) and at the Kristiansand Theatre, University of Agder, Norway (28-20 Aug 2017) producing further branch scores. A SoTL analysis of Speculations was presented at ISSoTL17 in Calgary, October 2017. Recalibrated through intense peer-review, a ‘Scroll Score’ of the generative composition to date was published as an open educational resource (OER) for ISSoTL17 (12 & 14 Oct 2017) and published on shift-work.org.ukShift/Work: Speculations is an innovative methodology that synthesises practice-based and practice-led research methods to transform our understanding and knowledge of artistic research (AR). It develops powerful insights into how Peer-2-Peer methods transmute speculative artistic practices by coupling the taking of risks with experiencing their consequences. Speculations combines new theories of paragogy with SoTL (Scholarship of Teaching & Learning) and Participatory Action Research (PAR) methods to develop and enhance a metacognitive understanding of AR. Through this, it invents a new theoretical framework - the ‘paratechnic’ - a means to collectively ‘score’ and disseminate artistic research as an OER. This is of particular importance to widening participation in the arts and restoring their civic purpose.‘Speculation’ is a unifying ethics (or cognitive bias) in AR commonly expressed as ‘without a script’ or ‘not knowing’. Drawing explicit attention to an implicit ethics within AR, and exposing it to the scrutiny and practices of non-artistic learners, raises awareness of its operations and limitations. This, in turn, enables us to repurpose, invent and practice metacognitive forms of speculation that have operational significance for, and beyond, AR.Speculations (Punctum) and newmaterialism.eu have been pivotal in suggesting ludic and non-anthropocentric forms of emergence that might foreground, and move beyond, AR's cognitive biases. Generative Shift/Work composition activates material probes as autopoetic catalysts for problem creation. As component interactions made radically distinct objects from the same material, speculation enabled Shift/Workers to formulate the concepts, equipment, and techniques to generate the truly collaborative ability to fabricate common research objects.Originality:Speculations is an original contribution to artistic knowledge, art andragogy and artistic research that implements emerging methods in paragogy and pioneers SoTL in art. A theoretically reflexive, participatory, and openly accessible paragogy for artistic research, Speculations liberates artistic knowledges by common-ing the proprietary ‘secret skills’ of the guild-monotechnic.Significance:Speculations has broad political, ontological and epistemological significance. Establishing a collective ontology for art practice though paragogy, Speculations exemplifies collectivist whole-systems thinking. Speculative research methods recognise that art is a subsystem of society - rather than separate from it - and ensure it has a pragmatic sense of its transformative potential.Rigour:Speculations is a scholarly, coherent, iterative system of meta-cognitive peer review. Composition is scaffolded with an academic and artistic community of ‘Shift/Workers’. Shift/Workers compose and play-test each other’s workshop scores before calibrating them through collective peer-review. Scores are then re-performed, iteratively, at international peer-reviewed artistic and scholarly events.
title: Unlearning Scroll Score

summary: This record contains the replication package accompanying the article “DCMT-Cert: Empirical Adequacy Certification of Machine-Learning Data-Contract Gates.” The package provides the scripts, retained numerical outputs, analysis tables, audit materials, dataset manifests, source hashes, and checksum information required to reproduce and inspect the computational analyses reported in the article. The materials cover the paired clean-versus-clean harm calibration, the Stage 1 policy-development analysis, the Stage 2 confirmation analysis, all five prespecified operating profiles, policy selection and multiplicity analyses, baseline comparisons, broadened fault analyses, model-family validation, native Great Expectations validation, harm-threshold sensitivity, provenance and transfer audits, and supporting consistency checks. The package is organised using descriptive file names and is intended to permit independent inspection and reproduction of the reported computational results. The accompanying article defines the experimental protocol, scope of the empirical certificates, statistical interpretation, and limitations of the study.
title: Replication Package for "DCMT-Cert: Empirical Adequacy Certification of Machine-Learning Data-Contract Gates"

summary: The Visibility Problem Hypershape Shadow Hypothesis II   Chloe J. Tully https://orcid.org/0009-0007-5661-7332 HSH Paper 1 https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23010822 Project UAP Studies   v0.1 3 October 2026 Preprint. Not peer-reviewed.   Companion to HSH I (28 September 2026). Tier-2 material is not in this paper.     DISCIPLINE   HSH I derived a geometry and assumed a flux law. This paper keeps the geometry and splits the assumption. What is proved is proved about the toy model. What is not selected — a coupling, a bulk metric, a relativistic completion — is named and left open. Neural coupling and retrocausality are still excluded. They are not implied by anything below.     ABSTRACT   HSH I predicted a parabolic light curve by taking received flux proportional to the area of the brane slice. That step is not geometry. For a 4-ball translating along the hidden axis, orthographic area scales as ρ² and reproduces the parabola F₂ = 1 − (t/τ)². Uniform emission through the 3-volume of the same slice scales as ρ³ and produces F₃ = [1 − (t/τ)²]^(3/2). The families meet at onset, peak, and end, and disagree in the shoulders: at |t/τ| = 1/√2, F₂ = 1/2 while F₃ = 1/(2√2). Calibrated photometry can tell them apart.   A 4-ellipsoid at fixed orientation in the XW plane stays inside both families, for every line of sight. An orientation that changes during the transit need not. One computed counterexample is given. The C₅ cover twist proposed in open problem O5 — cross-edges (i, 0) ↔ (i+1, 1) in place of the self-steps — is isomorphic to the untwisted cover, so the 1/φ gap is unchanged. No uniform self-step weight puts the even sector on the five-value spectrum flagged in HSH I. Coupling remains the critical open problem. Ansätze are stated with kill criteria. None is adopted.     CONTENTS   1. What HSH I already fixed 2. Two measures, two light curves 3. Fixed orientation stays parabolic 4. The C₅ twist does not close O5 5. Coupling ansätze, none chosen 6. What this does not unlock 7. Status of claims

summary: Mathematics, as taught in schools, has historically been presented as a universal, neutral, and decontextualized body of knowledge, contributing to the maintenance of exclusionary and Eurocentric curricular practices. This conception ignores the plurality of ways of producing, organizing, and using mathematical knowledge in different cultural groups, generating processes of alienation and school failure, especially among students whose experiences do not align with the hegemonic mathematical culture. This article discusses Ethnomathematics as a theoretical-methodological perspective and research program, an indispensable epistemological and formative field in the initial training of mathematics teachers. The objective is to analyze how Ethnomathematics can be integrated into the undergraduate mathematics curriculum, to enable future teachers to recognize, value, and articulate mathematical knowledge from different cultural groups with academic mathematics, promoting an inclusive, critical, and socially committed education. To this end, it is based on several theoretical frameworks that encompass Ethnomathematics, teacher training, and critical pedagogical approaches, such as those of Freire and Skovsmose. After investigations, readings, and rereading, it is concluded that the systematic integration of Ethnomathematics into initial teacher training contributes to the decolonization of the curriculum, the humanization of mathematics teaching, and the training of reflective teachers committed to social justice.
title: ETHNOMATHEMATICS AS A THEORETICAL AND METHODOLOGICAL PERSPECTIVE IN THE INITIAL TRAINING OF MATHEMATICS TEACHERS

summary: Analysis-ready aggregate data for a systematic review and meta-analysis comparing decompressive craniectomy more than 48 hours versus within 48 hours after onset in malignant middle cerebral artery infarction. Version 3 contains data and provenance records only. Contents: two-by-two counts for mortality (14 studies) and unfavorable functional outcome (12 studies) with exposure stratum, analysis role, outcome horizon and derivation; a cell-level provenance file giving, for every analyzed count, the extraction-workbook cell(s), their verbatim content and the arithmetic applied; arm-level counts by timing midpoint; and dual ROBINS-I ratings. Primary analysis (onset-to-surgery MCA cohorts; REML random effects with the modified Hartung-Knapp adjustment): mortality OR 1.136 (95% CI 0.705-1.832; k = 12; N = 585); unfavorable function OR 1.370 (0.812-2.313; k = 10; N = 511). Including the admission-timed administrative cohort and the mixed-territory cohort: 1.025 (0.800-1.314; k = 14) and 1.133 (0.896-1.434; k = 12). Changes from version 2: primary analysis restricted to onset-timed MCA cohorts; Shen 2024 mortality added; cell-level provenance added; figures and scripts removed.
title: Timing of decompressive craniectomy in malignant middle cerebral artery infarction: analysis-ready dataset and cell-level provenance for a systematic review and meta-analysis of surgery beyond 48 hours

summary: Data and Python code accompanying the manuscript “Replication-Based Criteria Can Change the Selected Number of Clusters: A Seven-Criterion Audit of k-Means on Indonesian Provincial Environmental Data” (submitted to the Journal of Computing Theories and Applications). The package audits how the number of clusters, k, is selected for k-means on a small tabular dataset: the published components of Indonesia’s Environmental Quality Index (Indeks Kualitas Lingkungan Hidup) for 38 provinces, 2021–2024. Seven criteria are computed for k = 2 to 8: the within-cluster sum of squares (read visually and by two formal knee rules), silhouette width, the Davies–Bouldin and Calinski–Harabasz indices, the gap statistic, subsample stability (adjusted Rand index over 200 pairs of overlapping 80% subsamples) and agreement with Ward linkage. The scripts also run sensitivity analyses, a comparison of six clustering algorithms, fixed-centroid assignment across years, a leave-one-out comparison of regression models for the air quality component, permutation importance and exact Shapley values. Contents: data/ (index components 2021–2024; GRDP per capita and population density; a cell-level provenance audit), code/ (six analysis scripts and a plotting-style module), README.md (run order, variable dictionary and data sources), requirements.txt (pinned library versions), CITATION.cff and licence files. Running the six scripts in the order given in README.md reproduces every table and figure of the manuscript in about four minutes on a laptop (Python 3.11 or later). The indicator values are official statistics from Statistics Indonesia (Badan Pusat Statistik) and are reproduced unchanged. Please cite the original BPS tables as well as this record. summary: Privacy-derived scientific materials for controlled studies of evidence access and adverse product content in AI assessment. The supplement contains synthetic materials, prompts, recorded model answers, terminal failures, assignment mappings, original stage-specific scoring and statistical implementations, reference results, and an offline CPU replay entrypoint. It includes the main local studies, the hosted-model study, historical screening, two common-interface qualification rounds, and the exploratory two-model pilot. Screening and development records are kept distinct from formal comparisons; reused answer aliases are not independent generations. The qualification amendment was made after qualification and before the exploratory pilot, and the subsequent proposed formal extension was not run. The findings do not establish a general advantage of pre-event defense, equivalence, or broad robustness. CPU replay reproduces scores and statistics from the released scientific records; it does not regenerate answers or repeat the original private token/authorization/environment audits.

summary: This release contains the research artifacts for “Trustworthy Evaluation Frameworks for AI-Assisted Painting Restoration,” a master’s thesis at the University of Applied Sciences Technikum Wien. The study develops and applies an evidence-based evaluation framework combining traditional image quality metrics with perceptual, colour, texture, boundary, structural, robustness, and generative-uncertainty evidence. The Controlled-300 study covers 300 paintings across five categories, with 3,425 registered cases and 2,620 eligible cases. Four methods: OpenCV Telea, LaMa, HINT, and Stable Diffusion, provide 10,480 matched primary candidates. The broader reporting collection contains 13,879 retained candidates. Additional investigations include 1,025 four-seed Stable Diffusion uncertainty groups, damage-size sensitivity, mask robustness, synthetic degradation, and separate diagnostic studies. SDXL is included as a bounded feasibility investigation, not as a fifth full-coverage method. Across 2,320 matched non-zero-damage cases, LaMa achieved the best mean masked MAE (14.83) and crop LPIPS (0.1292), while Telea achieved the best mean crop SSIM (0.8632). These complementary results motivate examining restoration quality through multiple forms of saved evidence. The archive brings together source code, notebooks, configurations, painting provenance, experimental outputs, candidate restorations, diagnostic maps, metric tables, reports, and supporting documentation. An accompanying eight room Streamlit dashboard presents the saved findings interactively. Release manifests and checksums document the archived files. Model weights and execution environments are not included. Licensing and third-party exclusions are described in the accompanying rights notice. Download and extraction: The research archive is distributed as eight numbered parts ( .zip.001 to .zip.008 ). Download all eight parts and follow REASSEMBLE.txt to reconstruct and verify the original ZIP before extraction. The parts are not independently extractable archives. SPLIT_MANIFEST.json records each part’s size and checksums; SHA256SUMS.txt covers the uploaded files. Splitting changes only the delivery format: the research contents remain unchanged.   Source code and documentation Interactive research dashboard Candidate restoration repository Diagnostics repository

summary: Added Added SNS, SQS and ECR permissions to ASF-deployment-ci-cf.yml for deploying HyP3-backed monitoring stacks. New deployments: pism-cloud-sandbox , hyp3-beta-test , hyp3-beta , hyp3-pse-watermaps-test , and hyp3-pse-watermaps . Added a PISM_ISMIP7_GREENLAND_RUN job for preparing both forward and inverse model runs of Greenland for ISMIP7. Added the ntasks API parameter to PISM_EXECUTE so vCPUs and memory can be dynamically set from job parameters. A GLACIER_MELT job, which is made available in hyp3-beta, for computing melt extents and snowlines from glacier backscatter images. Changed The maximum length of the bucket_prefix job parameter has been increased to 700 UTF-8 characters from 100. ARTRAFF_RTC (MultiRTC) jobs now take a floating point number instead of an integer for the resolution parameter. The minimum of 0 is also now correctly represented as an exclusive minimum (must be > 0, not ≥ ). Combined the PISM_TERRA_RUN_FORWARD and PISM_TERRA_RUN_INERVERSE jobs into PISM_GLACIER_RUN job for preparing both forward and inverse model runs of RGI glacier complexes. Renamed the PISM_TERRA_EXECUTE job to PISM_EXECUTE in line with the other PISM jobs. Removed required RGI subdirectory from the run_script S3 URI parameter in the PISM_EXECUTE job type generalizing it for non-glaicer runs. all PISM_* jobs will now set their vCPU and memory requirements via batch container overrides using the ntasks job parameter, which now has a maximum of 192 tasks (corresponding to a r8id.48xlarge ). The timeout for all PISM jobs has been extended to 1 week. Increased default/expanded vCPUs to 13000 for all PSIM deployments. Reworked custom HyP3 deployment actions JPL deployments have been moved to the deploy-custom-jpl-test.yml and deploy-custom-jpl-prod.yml workflows so they can keep using service user access keys. Remaining HyP3 deployments in the delpoy-custom-test.yml and deploy-custom-prod.yml workflows are now deployed via OIDC. All references to the HyP3 CI/CD stack name has been changed to github-actions from hyp3-ci inline with typical usage. Reduced default/expanded vCPUs to 1000/2000 in hyp3-edc-uat and hyp3-edc-prod.

summary: Replication package of a bibliometric review of data science, predictive analytics and recommender systems in international trade and market demand (Scopus, 2015–2025). summary: Replication package for a study of whether the adoption of autonomous coding agents spreads through open-source collaboration networks. The package rebuilds every number, table and figure in the paper from two public sources: the AIDev dataset of agent-authored pull requests (Hugging Face, hao-li/AIDev) and GH Archive (Google BigQuery public dataset). Neither source is redistributed here. Contents: the BigQuery query used to extract weekly developer-repository activity; Python scripts for adoption-event extraction, dynamic co-activity network construction, person-week panel building, discrete-time hazard models, five identification tests (within-week comparison, propensity matching, timing permutation, future-tie placebos, and exposure split by agent), a calibrated agent-based seeding simulation, and figure generation; and the resulting tables as CSV and JSON. Study scope: 282,626 developers across 17,353 repositories over 30 weeks of 2025, with 2,250 first-adoption events. Requires Python 3.10+ with pandas, pyarrow, numpy, scipy, statsmodels, scikit-learn, igraph, matplotlib and pillow, plus a Google Cloud project with BigQuery access. See README.md for the run order.

summary: Preprocessed human GRCh38 reference database for fusion-function, based on Ensembl release 100, with InterPro, PANTHER and reviewed human UniProt annotations. The compact SQLite database contains sequences, prepared transcript/CDS coordinates, splice-site annotations and protein features for predicting fusion reading frames and feature retention. It omits raw Ensembl tables and cannot regenerate annotations using --preprocess-only . Build 1. The accompanying manifest records compatibility metadata, sizes, SHA-256 checksums and source provenance. Source-specific attribution and reuse conditions are described in LICENSES-ensembl-100.txt. Software and documentation: https://github.com/creisle/fusion_function

summary: Supplementary data and code accompanying the manuscript “An Evidence-Chain Provenance Framework for Tracing the Overseas Circulation of Oracle Bones: A GIS-Based Approach”. This package provides materials for editors and referees to check the study’s methods and results. It includes: (i) the Tier A–D evidence-classification coding scheme; (ii) circulation-pathway tables and CSV files aligned with Tables 1–3; (iii) record-level evidence codes underlying Fig. 6; (iv) an English evidence-ledger digest; (v) a bilingual Chinese–English concordance of cited Chinese-language sources and personal names; (vi) location notes for GIS visualizations; (vii) Python scripts used to generate Figs. 1–6; (viii) finished figure PNGs matching the manuscript; and (ix) a public-domain Natural Earth basemap for re-running Fig. 5. The study synthesizes published historical sources, museum catalogues, and publicly disclosed institutional records. No new laboratory, survey, or interview datasets were generated. Author-generated materials are shared under CC BY 4.0; copyrighted verbatim text of published sources is cited but not reproduced in full. Natural Earth data are public domain.

summary: Berggren's three matrices generate the tree of primitive Pythagorean triples and preserve the quadratic form x₁² + x₂² − x₃². Cha, Nguyen and Tauber (2018) built such trees for other integral ternary forms Q of signature (2,1). We ask whether the matrices alone determine Q. Main results: Recovery criterion (Theorem 3.1). A set of isometries of Q determines Q up to scale exactly when no nonzero vector is sent to plus or minus itself by all of them. Equivalently, the group they generate is not virtually abelian; for integral isometries, it acts irreducibly. The proof is elementary linear algebra and applies to arbitrary real groups. Berggren trees (Theorem 3.2, Proposition 3.3, Remark 3.5). Any two generators determine Q in Berggren's tree and in each of the five trees of Cha, Nguyen and Tauber. The definition of a Berggren tree alone does not force this: the generators A and A² give a Berggren forest for x₁² + x₂² − x₃² whose two generators both yield edges but do not determine Q. Roots at a rational null line (Theorem 3.6). For a primitive null vector P with divisor G, the minimum of Q on (P^⊥ ∩ ℤ³) \ ℤP is S = |det(2J)|/(2G²). An explicit congruence, Gm ≡ −τ (mod S), decides which minimal vectors e + mP are roots. N-cusps (Theorems 3.7–3.8, Corollary 3.9). For Q = ax₁² + bx₁x₂ + cx₂² − Nx₃² with D = b² − 4ac < 0, all data at the null vectors (p, q, 1) are explicit. A minimal root exists there if and only if gcd(G, S) divides D/G, and in particular whenever D is cube-free. Recovery by integral reflections (Theorem 3.12, Proposition 3.13). Minimal roots at two or three distinct rational null lines yield three integral reflections that determine Q. The paper also relates the reflections in the trees of Cha, Nguyen and Tauber to minimal roots (Remark 3.17), and states an open question for trees produced by their construction.

The chain begins with the generalized relative entropy Lean verifies that equal-mass inputs reduce this functional to finite Kullback–Leibler divergence. The previously verified Chronos EN1–EN6 complete-coarse-graining Arrow increment and rate are then connected directly to this D_+ functional. An explicit calibration interface links the entropy Arrow to the older Chronos Change/Arrow/Action clock system without assuming that the two independently defined Arrow quantities are identical. The bridge is subsequently lifted from scalar expressions to diagonal matrices and traces. in the diagonal spectral representation. Similarity invariance is then formally established, removing dependence on the chosen basis. The final CEG6 stage instantiates the construction using Mathlib's finite Hermitian spectral theorem for an arbitrary positive-definite real matrix G. The canonical eigenvector unitary, its two-sided inverse, strictly positive eigenvalues, the operator-trace identity, and the scaled finite spectral Lambda relation are all kernel checked. All final stages, CEG0 v0.5, CEG1 v0.3, CEG2 v0.3, CEG3 v0.2, CEG4 v0.2, CEG5 v0.2, and CEG6 v0.1, passed static placeholder audits and Lean axiom audits. The audited theorem dependencies report only propext , Classical.choice , and Quot.sound , with no sorryAx . The archive establishes a finite-dimensional mathematical compatibility chain. It does not assume that a Chronos physical state and an external geometric G-field are physically identical; where such a cross-framework state identification is required, the compatibility condition remains explicit in the formalization. Description This updated release extends the Lean-Verified Chronos Entropy–Gravity Bridge from CEG0–CEG6 through the new CEG7 field-to-measurement stage. The cumulative formal program connects the Chronos temporal framework to entropy production, generalized relative entropy, matrix and operator structure, positive-definite spectral geometry, gravity, and now an explicit experimentally testable prediction. The earlier CEG0–CEG6 stages formally established a chain from the Chronos entropy Arrow through generalized relative entropy into a finite positive-definite operator representation. The later stages removed dependence on a chosen basis and used Mathlib’s spectral theorem to connect the construction to arbitrary finite positive-definite real matrices. CEG7 adds the next important step. It connects the previously verified Chronos radial time field and its Newtonian gravity correspondence to a proposed gradient-dependent effective gravitational coupling. This produces a concrete predicted environmental shift in the measured gravitational coupling rather than only reproducing the standard Newtonian limit. The package also includes a formally verified comparison with a constant-coupling baseline. Lean proves that the constant baseline produces no environmental shift, while the Chronos model can produce a nonzero field-dependent shift. An explicit measurement-resolution theorem is included, showing the conditions under which an experiment would be able to distinguish the Chronos prediction from the zero-shift baseline. The cumulative CEG0–CEG7 chain therefore connects: Chronos temporal field → gravity → entropy → information structure → positive-definite operator geometry → measurable gravitational prediction. All final stages included in this release passed Lean verification in the pinned environment. Static source audits found no sorry , admit , o

summary: This paper proposes a modified special–relativistic framework in which rest energy is carried by the temporal component of the Minkowski metric through a scalar ζ= e −φ , realized as a dilaton that couples to matter through the temporal leg of the metric alone. A particle is postulated to convert—by a graviton–mediated process with cycle energy E= A/f—between a massive (ζ →0) and a massless (ζ = 1) state, reaching the light–speed limit without the usual infinite–energy obstruction. Part I develops the framework: the temporal mass term, the conversion oscillation, graviton kinematics derived from four–momentum conservation, a covariant (disformal, preferred–frame) action for the temporal dilaton, and a modified Einstein equation that covariant conservation forces back to general relativity. Part II, more speculatively, identifies ζ 2 with the inverse of the temporal element G int of the pentadimensional Deformed Space–Time (DST) metrics of gravity and the strong interaction (ζ 2 = 1/G int ; the electroweak metrics are read as the luminal ζ = 1 branch), used strictly as a phenomenological parametrization; extends the geometry to a Calabi–Yau threefold (the T 6 /Z 3 orbifold worked out explicitly; three generations require discrete Wilson lines on it or a different manifold); and proposes a dictionary between Standard–Model particles, features of that manifold, and a tetrahedral nuclear model, resting on numerical correspondences rather than derivations. Confrontation with data is stated as four survival conditions (S1–S4): the temporal scalar must be short–ranged (m φ ≳5 meV); planetary ephemerides bound the conversion constant, f esc A≲5 ×10 −31 W per nucleon (f esc the radiated fraction of a cycle); ordinary matter cannot feed the dark sector at cosmological rates; and the dark–sector conjecture survives only as a dark–sector–internal exchange tied to an evolving w(z). The one laboratory target is an α ≈ 2 Yukawa correction to gravity at λ ≈ 4–10 µm with no equivalence–principle violation. A closing section reads the author’s movie of cellular convection on the surface of hot water as a kinematic analogue of the cosmic web (an Analogy, not evidence), gives the dark–sector exchange its interacting–dark–energy form, and adds a fifth survival condition (S5: any variation of Gconfined to the dark sector) and a survey target (T2); the analogy itself is evidence for none of these.
title: Energy and Spacetime Revised and Expanded Edition (v13): Standard–Model Alignment and a Six–Dimensional Calabi–Yau Extension

summary: We give an explicit convex polygon with 63 rational vertices whose area, after its shortest closed Euclidean billiard length is normalized to one, is smaller than that of Mallée’s parabolic triangle. This disproves Conjecture 2.2 of Balitskiy, Mitrofanov and Polyanskii (2026). The polygon was found by moving supporting lines near the parabolic triangle’s focal contacts and then discretizing the resulting shape. The proof checks the literal polygon in exact rational arithmetic: 63 width directions and all 39,711 triples of supporting edge lines. A three-file verification package contains the coordinates and an independent checker. The result identifies a better competitor, without claiming that it is optimal.
title: A rational polygonal counterexample to the Mallée parabolic triangle conjecture

summary: The Sardinian Priestly Diaspora and the Roots of the Classical Pantheon From the Gallurese Architectural-Tumulus Koiné to the Pan-European Spread of the Cults of Apollo and Athena https://www.luigiusai.it/ontology/rotta-aristeica/index.html Abstract This paper proposes an interpretive framework to reassess the role of protohistoric Sardinia in European cultural, religious, and architectural genesis. It advances the hypothesis that Sardinian seafaring groups led by lineages of warrior-priests undertook early migration routes toward the continent, establishing a constellation of satellite settlements and communities that preserved mutual networks of contact and shared identity through a common linguistic matrix over time. Within this diasporic horizon lies the pan-European and Mediterranean dissemination of the cults of primordial divine figures, subsequently integrated into the Greek pantheon as Apollo and Athena: The archetype of the sacred archer: The iconographic genesis of Apollo finds its material and devotional referent in Sardinian bronze statuary ( bronzetti ) depicting archers, situated within a chronological and stylistic dialogue with the Mycenaean horizon. Athena Tritonis and Sardinian topography: The cult of Athena is traced back to the hydrographic and sacred landscape of southern Sardinia, identifying the historical Lake Tritonis with the wetland lagoon area of modern-day Cagliari. Metallurgical continuity: As demonstrated in the analytical investigation by Usai (2026), these archetypes maintained a trans-epochal persistence codified in traditional Sardinian wrought-iron craftsmanship (unconscious metallurgical memory and Scythian volutes). At the material and settlement level, this work addresses the issue of posthumous toponymic fragmentation. The same hypogeic construction matrix—exemplified on the island by the Domus de Janas —was recorded locally under disparate designations that obscured its typological unity (ranging from French Grottes des Fées to rock-cut manifestations in Lydia). Similarly, a direct correlation is posited between the Gallurese megalithic circles/tumuli and the emergence of the wider "Tumulus Culture," understood as the manifestation of migratory trajectories originating with Gallurese populations and their descendants, who perpetuated identical ritual and funerary customs. The purpose of this preprint lies in the methodological necessity of formally organizing intuitions and convergences that have preliminarily emerged across independent research circles and public dissemination channels, consolidating them into a unified, citable theoretical framework open to official scientific inquiry. Research Theses Overview (Body of Text) 1. Migratory Networks and the Linguistic Koiné of Warrior-Priests The Sardinian expansion across Europe did not constitute an accidental or fragmented colonization, but a coordinated movement guided by seafaring priestly and warrior elites. Small settlements established along coastal and fluvial routes maintained enduring communication networks, whose cohesion was sustained through a shared language and common ceremonial codes. 2. Architectural Homogeneity and Toponymic Aberration The failure to recognize continental Sardinian diffusion stems largely from local linguistic divergence and regional folklore: Ritual Hypogeism: The rock-cut structures known in Sardinia as Domus de Janas correspond directly to complexes across Atlantic Europe (e.g., Grottes des Fées or hypogeic dolmens) and western Anatolia (Lydia), cataloged under isolated classifications solely due to modern regional or folkloric designations. Gallurese Tumuli as the Primary Matrix: The widespread Tumulus Culture on continental and extra-European scales finds its genesis and prototype in the megalithic horizon of Gallura, propagated through successive migrations that preserved identical building paradigms and mortuary rituals. 3. Cult Transmission: Apollo and A
title: Apollo and Athena were Sardinian gods

summary: The ATLAS observation of impact-parameter-dependent nuclear parton distributions provides empirical confirmation of a foundational principle of topological soliton models: hadronic structure functions are not immutable point-particle distributions, but scale-dependent spectral projections of localized vortex loops coupled to the background vacuum density. Because the vacuum substrate is compressible, dense nuclear packing induces a localized density depletion in the nuclear core, compressing the aspect ratio of embedded Borromean solitons and generating the classical EMC suppression. At the nuclear periphery (bA ≥ RA), the local density depression vanishes exponentially, and the solitons recover their unperturbed vacuum ground-state aspect ratio Λ0. Consequently, nucleons residing in the nuclear skin behave as unmodified free nucleons. The resulting analytical ratio R(x+) ∝ 1/⟨RA(x+)⟩core directly reproduces the 21.4% monotonic rise and the 6.0σ signal observed by ATLAS without introducing unconstrained empirical parameters.
title: Substrate Compressibility in Topological Soliton Nucleons: An Analytical Benchmark of the ATLAS 5.02 TeV Photonuclear Measurement

Because the vacuum substrate is compressible, dense nuclear packing induces a localized density depletion in the nuclear core, compressing the aspect ratio of embedded Borromean solitons and generating the classical EMC suppression. At the nuclear periphery (bA ≥ RA), the local density depression vanishes exponentially, and the solitons recover their unperturbed vacuum ground-state aspect ratio Λ0. Consequently, nucleons residing in the nuclear skin behave as unmodified free nucleons. The resulting analytical ratio R(x+) ∝ 1/⟨RA(x+)⟩core directly reproduces the 21.4% monotonic rise and the 6.0σ signal observed by ATLAS without introducing unconstrained empirical parameters.

summary: Lean 4 formalisation of root-moment rigidity and the forced-factor step in a parity descent for the Lai-Sprang function-field Littlewood series. Includes exact-certificate soundness, named coefficient streams, polynomial/Laurent coefficient and fractional-product bridges, and reproducible exact finite-field experiments.   The included ordinary proof establishes the auxiliary all-shift bound j-d <= N for d < N(N-1), with N=2^v_2(p-1). This cutoff is not yet an end-to-end Lean theorem: the root enumeration, coefficient-window-to-moment derivation and complete descent remain separate obligations. The all-degree auxiliary bound and characteristic-two frontier remain unresolved.   The parity/Vandermonde/nonsquare method is attributed to Li Lai and Johannes Sprang, arXiv:2606.00633v1, Section 3. First-formalisation priority and independent human peer review are not claimed. OpenAI Codex was used extensively under Greg Baker's research direction. See NOTICE and releases/v0.1.0.md for provenance, exact hypotheses and reproduction instructions.

summary: Code, partition manifests and per-image predictions supporting the audit and leakage-controlled re-evaluation of the 4,217-image Eye Disease Retinal Images collection.   Contents: the provenance and integrity audit; the manifests defining every evaluation arm image by image (image-level, patient-grouped, size-matched, source-matched, the common test set and the six leave-one-source-out splits); the training and evaluation code; stored per-image class probabilities for every run; the shortcut probes; and the visual adjudication verdicts for all 335 cross-label near-duplicate candidates.   The image collection itself is not redistributed here. It is available at https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/python16/eye-disease-retinal-images and the manifests reference it by relative path.

summary: EnvGeo-Seawater v1.3.4 EnvGeo-Seawater is an interactive Python and Streamlit platform for exploring seawater isotope and hydrographic data. This stable release combines a core collection of more than 2,000 seawater isotope measurements from around Japan, analyzed under harmonized analytical criteria, with external regional and global reference datasets. Together, the platform integrates approximately 50,000 cited records, including NASA GISS and PAGES CoralHydro2k reference datasets. It provides mapping, 2D–4D visualization, salinity–isotope relationships, T–S diagrams, depth profiles, vertical sections, and session-only comparison with user-supplied data. Installation python -m pip install envgeo-seawater envgeo-seawater For Apple Silicon macOS, install proj, pyproj, and cartopy from conda-forge before installing the package. See the README for details. Documentation Online user guide: https://envgeo.github.io/seawater_map/ Source repository: https://github.com/envgeo/seawater_map PyPI package: https://pypi.org/project/envgeo-seawater/1.3.4/ Citation and data sources Please cite EnvGeo-Seawater and the original data providers used in an analysis. Dataset provenance and third-party notices are documented in the repository. This release contains stable public pages 03, 04, 05, 31, 32, 34, 35, 37, 53, and historical archive page 80. Development pages 90/91 and local diagnostic page 99 are excluded.
title: EnvGeo-Seawater: An Interactive Platform for Exploring Seawater Isotope and Hydrographic Data

summary: <!-- release-title: v1.17.0: 研究助理 --> wisp-science v1.17.0 — Research Assistant Keep one conversation for your research plans, delegate work to projects, and receive the results on your desktop or in WeChat. The new Research assistant brings project activity, saved plans and task dispatch into one persistent conversation. Ask what happened this week, record today's priorities, or send a concrete task to a project conversation. The assistant coordinates the work; project agents perform the analysis. This release also adds daily research recaps, an Automation page, configurable hooks, and improvements to conversation controls and the native desktop previews. Downloads macOS : signed and notarized DMG installers for Apple Silicon and Intel; compatible installations can update in-app. macOS SwiftUI Preview : separate signed and notarized DMG installers for Apple Silicon and Intel, each with a SHA-256 checksum. Windows : MSI and NSIS installers. Windows release signing is currently disabled, so these installers remain unsigned. Linux : deb and AppImage packages for x86_64 and aarch64. Installers will appear in Assets as the platform builds finish. The Windows WinUI 3 preview remains available through native-preview workflow artifacts or a local source build; it does not replace the regular Windows installer. Research assistant Open Research assistant from the home screen, replacing the former scratch-chat entry. It keeps one ongoing conversation across projects, with independently collapsible project and calendar sidebars. Narrow windows use drawers. Ask for recorded progress across visible projects, or select one project to include its saved conversations in subsequent questions. Projects hidden by privacy mode remain unavailable to the assistant. Save dated plans with open, done or dropped states. Unfinished items carry forward to today, and plans survive conversation compaction. List project conversations, continue an existing conversation or create one for a task. A requested server can become that conversation's default execution context before dispatch; a busy conversation is not interrupted or rebound. Once a project agent accepts the task, the assistant acknowledges startup and becomes available again. When the project turn ends, a background summary reports the result, output files, failures and unfinished work in the assistant conversation. Project approvals for dispatched work are reviewed against the original request. Clear operations within that request can be approved once; uncertainty or incomplete details are forwarded to you. Assistant Full Permission does not grant project-wide permission. The assistant does not itself edit files, run commands or search literature. Those actions belong to the project agents it dispatches. See the research assistant guide and tutorial . WeChat access Research assistant → Remote access provides its own opt-in WeChat iLink binding. Messages reach the same assistant conversation without switching projects with slash commands. This binding is independent from the project bot in Settings. A bot can belong to only one entry at a time, and only its bound owner's private messages are accepted. Reply yes or no to the current approval, use full / full off for the assistant conversation's temporary Full Permission, and use /approval to show a pending request again. Full Permission resets when Wisp restarts. Tasks started through WeChat send their completion summaries back to the original binding. /status , /help and /stop stay within the assistant entry. Keep Wisp running for remote access and completion callbacks. If iLink's reply window expires, the summary is saved on the desktop and queued for the next message on the same connection. Quitting Wisp or unbinding can discard pending in-memory notifications. A finished agent turn is not proof that a separately submitted long-running job has finished. Recaps, automation and hooks The new Automation page brings project schedules and daily

summary: Abstract: Efficient sensing remains critical in low-cost Internet of Things (IoT) and Web of Things (WoT)-enabled edge nodes, even when the sensor itself is inexpensive and widely used. The DHT11 temperature and humidity sensor employs a single-wire dig-ital protocol and relies on Arduino libraries for data acquisition, timeout handling, and scheduling behavior. In this paper, eight Arduino DHT11 libraries are benchmarked on an Arduino Uno R3 using six criteria: flash memory usage, SRAM consumption, average measured call duration, timing variability, maximum CPU blocking time, and failure-recovery behavior. The results reveal substantial performance trade-offs. Aver-age measured call durations ranged from 5,588 µs for the asynchronous DHT Sensors Non-Blocking implementation to approximately 1.04 s for DHT11; however, these measurements reflect different execution semantics and should not be interpreted as directly equivalent end-to-end acquisition latencies. Flash usage ranged from 4,288 to 5,244 bytes, while SRAM consumption ranged from 238 to 266 bytes. TroykaDHT and SDHT delivered the most stable low-latency readings, DFRobot_DHT11 minimized SRAM usage, and DHT Sensors Non-Blocking was most suitable when asynchronous execution and reduced continuous CPU occupation were required. This study does not directly benchmark application-layer protocols or cloud services, such as HTTP, MQTT, REST, or WebSocket; instead, it characterizes sensing-layer behavior that can influence data freshness, task scheduling, and overall responsiveness in resource-constrained IoT/WoT edge deployments.
title: Performance Analysis of Arduino DHT11 Sensor Libraries for Resource-constrained IoT/WoT Edge Nodes.

summary: Data and Python code accompanying the manuscript “Replication-Based Criteria Can Change the Selected Number of Clusters: A Seven-Criterion Audit of k-Means on Indonesian Provincial Environmental Data” (submitted to the Journal of Computing Theories and Applications). The package audits how the number of clusters, k, is selected for k-means on a small tabular dataset: the published components of Indonesia’s Environmental Quality Index (Indeks Kualitas Lingkungan Hidup) for 38 provinces, 2021–2024. Seven criteria are computed for k = 2 to 8: the within-cluster sum of squares (read visually and by two formal knee rules), silhouette width, the Davies–Bouldin and Calinski–Harabasz indices, the gap statistic, subsample stability (adjusted Rand index over 200 pairs of overlapping 80% subsamples) and agreement with Ward linkage. The scripts also run sensitivity analyses, a comparison of six clustering algorithms, fixed-centroid assignment across years, a leave-one-out comparison of regression models for the air quality component, permutation importance and exact Shapley values. Contents: data/ (index components 2021–2024; GRDP per capita and population density; a cell-level provenance audit), code/ (six analysis scripts and a plotting-style module), README.md (run order, variable dictionary and data sources), requirements.txt (pinned library versions), CITATION.cff and licence files. Running the six scripts in the order given in README.md reproduces every table and figure of the manuscript in about four minutes on a laptop (Python 3.11 or later). The indicator values are official statistics from Statistics Indonesia (Badan Pusat Statistik) and are reproduced unchanged. Please cite the original BPS tables as well as this record. Code: MIT licence. Data files: CC BY 4.0.

summary: Privacy-derived scientific materials for controlled studies of evidence access and adverse product content in AI assessment. The supplement contains synthetic materials, prompts, recorded model answers, terminal failures, assignment mappings, original stage-specific scoring and statistical implementations, reference results, and an offline CPU replay entrypoint. It includes the main local studies, the hosted-model study, historical screening, two common-interface qualification rounds, and the exploratory two-model pilot. Screening and development records are kept distinct from formal comparisons; reused answer aliases are not independent generations. The qualification amendment was made after qualification and before the exploratory pilot, and the subsequent proposed formal extension was not run. The findings do not establish a general advantage of pre-event defense, equivalence, or broad robustness. This is a redacted scientific derivative with a new integrity manifest: account authorizations, user dialogue, machine paths, hardware logs, original provider envelopes, encrypted reasoning, native token journals and model weights are excluded. CPU replay reproduces scores and statistics from the released scientific records; it does not regenerate answers or repeat the original private token/authorization/environment audits.
title: Scientific supplement for Evidence Access and Adverse Product Content in AI Assessment

summary: This release contains the research artifacts for “Trustworthy Evaluation Frameworks for AI-Assisted Painting Restoration,” a master’s thesis at the University of Applied Sciences Technikum Wien. The study develops and applies an evidence-based evaluation framework combining traditional image quality metrics with perceptual, colour, texture, boundary, structural, robustness, and generative-uncertainty evidence. The Controlled-300 study covers 300 paintings across five categories, with 3,425 registered cases and 2,620 eligible cases. Four methods: OpenCV Telea, LaMa, HINT, and Stable Diffusion, provide 10,480 matched primary candidates. The broader reporting collection contains 13,879 retained candidates. Additional investigations include 1,025 four-seed Stable Diffusion uncertainty groups, damage-size sensitivity, mask robustness, synthetic degradation, and separate diagnostic studies. SDXL is included as a bounded feasibility investigation, not as a fifth full-coverage method. Across 2,320 matched non-zero-damage cases, LaMa achieved the best mean masked MAE (14.83) and crop LPIPS (0.1292), while Telea achieved the best mean crop SSIM (0.8632). These complementary results motivate examining restoration quality through multiple forms of saved evidence. The archive brings together source code, notebooks, configurations, painting provenance, experimental outputs, candidate restorations, diagnostic maps, metric tables, reports, and supporting documentation. An accompanying eight room Streamlit dashboard presents the saved findings interactively. Release manifests and checksums document the archived files. Model weights and execution environments are not included. Licensing and third-party exclusions are described in the accompanying rights notice. Download and extraction: The research archive is distributed as eight numbered parts ( .zip.001 to .zip.008 ). Download all eight parts and follow REASSEMBLE.txt to reconstruct and verify the original ZIP before extraction. The parts are not independently extractable archives. SPLIT_MANIFEST.json records each part’s size and checksums; SHA256SUMS.txt covers the uploaded files. Splitting changes only the delivery format: the research contents remain unchanged.   Source code and documentation Interactive research dashboard Candidate restoration repository Diagnostics repository
title: Trustworthy Evaluation Frameworks for AI-Assisted Painting Restoration: Controlled-300 Research Artifacts

summary: Replication package for a study of whether the adoption of autonomous coding agents spreads through open-source collaboration networks. The package rebuilds every number, table and figure in the paper from two public sources: the AIDev dataset of agent-authored pull requests (Hugging Face, hao-li/AIDev) and GH Archive (Google BigQuery public dataset). Neither source is redistributed here. Contents: the BigQuery query used to extract weekly developer-repository activity; Python scripts for adoption-event extraction, dynamic co-activity network construction, person-week panel building, discrete-time hazard models, five identification tests (within-week comparison, propensity matching, timing permutation, future-tie placebos, and exposure split by agent), a calibrated agent-based seeding simulation, and figure generation; and the resulting tables as CSV and JSON. Study scope: 282,626 developers across 17,353 repositories over 30 weeks of 2025, with 2,250 first-adoption events. Requires Python 3.10+ with pandas, pyarrow, numpy, scipy, statsmodels, scikit-learn, igraph, matplotlib and pillow, plus a Google Cloud project with BigQuery access. See README.md for the run order.

It includes: (i) the Tier A–D evidence-classification coding scheme; (ii) circulation-pathway tables and CSV files aligned with Tables 1–3; (iii) record-level evidence codes underlying Fig. 6; (iv) an English evidence-ledger digest; (v) a bilingual Chinese–English concordance of cited Chinese-language sources and personal names; (vi) location notes for GIS visualizations; (vii) Python scripts used to generate Figs. 1–6; (viii) finished figure PNGs matching the manuscript; and (ix) a public-domain Natural Earth basemap for re-running Fig. 5. summary: Berggren's three matrices generate the tree of primitive Pythagorean triples and preserve the quadratic form x₁² + x₂² − x₃². Cha, Nguyen and Tauber (2018) built such trees for other integral ternary forms Q of signature (2,1). We ask whether the matrices alone determine Q. Main results: Recovery criterion (Theorem 3.1). A set of isometries of Q determines Q up to scale exactly when no nonzero vector is sent to plus or minus itself by all of them. Equivalently, the group they generate is not virtually abelian; for integral isometries, it acts irreducibly. The proof is elementary linear algebra and applies to arbitrary real groups. Berggren trees (Theorem 3.2, Proposition 3.3, Remark 3.5). Any two generators determine Q in Berggren's tree and in each of the five trees of Cha, Nguyen and Tauber. The definition of a Berggren tree alone does not force this: the generators A and A² give a Berggren forest for x₁² + x₂² − x₃² whose two generators both yield edges but do not determine Q. Roots at a rational null line (Theorem 3.6). For a primitive null vector P with divisor G, the minimum of Q on (P^⊥ ∩ ℤ³) \ ℤP is S = |det(2J)|/(2G²). An explicit congruence, Gm ≡ −τ (mod S), decides which minimal vectors e + mP are roots. N-cusps (Theorems 3.7–3.8, Corollary 3.9). For Q = ax₁² + bx₁x₂ + cx₂² − Nx₃² with D = b² − 4ac < 0, all data at the null vectors (p, q, 1) are explicit. A minimal root exists there if and only if gcd(G, S) divides D/G, and in particular whenever D is cube-free. Recovery by integral reflections (Theorem 3.12, Proposition 3.13). Minimal roots at two or three distinct rational null lines yield three integral reflections that determine Q. The paper also relates the reflections in the trees of Cha, Nguyen and Tauber to minimal roots (Remark 3.17), and states an open question for trees produced by their construction.
title: The Inverse Berggren Tree Problem

summary: This paper proposes a modified special–relativistic framework in which rest energy is carried by the temporal component of the Minkowski metric through a scalar ζ= e −φ , realized as a dilaton that couples to matter through the temporal leg of the metric alone. A particle is postulated to convert—by a graviton–mediated process with cycle energy E= A/f—between a massive (ζ →0) and a massless (ζ = 1) state, reaching the light–speed limit without the usual infinite–energy obstruction. Part I develops the framework: the temporal mass term, the conversion oscillation, graviton kinematics derived from four–momentum conservation, a covariant (disformal, preferred–frame) action for the temporal dilaton, and a modified Einstein equation that covariant conservation forces back to general relativity. Part II, more speculatively, identifies ζ 2 with the inverse of the temporal element G int of the pentadimensional Deformed Space–Time (DST) metrics of gravity and the strong interaction (ζ 2 = 1/G int ; the electroweak metrics are read as the luminal ζ = 1 branch), used strictly as a phenomenological parametrization; extends the geometry to a Calabi–Yau threefold (the T 6 /Z 3 orbifold worked out explicitly; three generations require discrete Wilson lines on it or a different manifold); and proposes a dictionary between Standard–Model particles, features of that manifold, and a tetrahedral nuclear model, resting on numerical correspondences rather than derivations. Confrontation with data is stated as four survival conditions (S1–S4): the temporal scalar must be short–ranged (m φ ≳5 meV); planetary ephemerides bound the conversion constant, f esc A≲5 ×10 −31 W per nucleon (f esc the radiated fraction of a cycle); ordinary matter cannot feed the dark sector at cosmological rates; and the dark–sector conjecture survives only as a dark–sector–internal exchange tied to an evolving w(z). The one laboratory target is an α ≈ 2 Yukawa correction to gravity at λ ≈ 4–10 µm with no equivalence–principle violation. A closing section reads the author’s movie of cellular convection on the surface of hot water as a kinematic analogue of the cosmic web (an Analogy, not evidence), gives the dark–sector exchange its interacting–dark–energy form, and adds a fifth survival condition (S5: any variation of Gconfined to the dark sector) and a survey target (T2); the analogy itself is evidence for none of these.
title: Energy and Spacetime Revised and Expanded Edition (v13): Standard–Model Alignment and a Six–Dimensional Calabi–Yau Extension

summary: The ATLAS observation of impact-parameter-dependent nuclear parton distributions provides empirical confirmation of a foundational principle of topological soliton models: hadronic structure functions are not immutable point-particle distributions, but scale-dependent spectral projections of localized vortex loops coupled to the background vacuum density. Because the vacuum substrate is compressible, dense nuclear packing induces a localized density depletion in the nuclear core, compressing the aspect ratio of embedded Borromean solitons and generating the classical EMC suppression. At the nuclear periphery (bA ≥ RA), the local density depression vanishes exponentially, and the solitons recover their unperturbed vacuum ground-state aspect ratio Λ0. Consequently, nucleons residing in the nuclear skin behave as unmodified free nucleons. The resulting analytical ratio R(x+) ∝ 1/⟨RA(x+)⟩core directly reproduces the 21.4% monotonic rise and the 6.0σ signal observed by ATLAS without introducing unconstrained empirical parameters.
title: Substrate Compressibility in Topological Soliton Nucleons: An Analytical Benchmark of the ATLAS 5.02 TeV Photonuclear Measurement
