summary: This record contains the complete supplementary aggregate-results and analysis-code archives for the manuscript "Associations of the triglyceride–glucose–body mass index with concurrent low bone and muscle mass depend on muscle mass definition: a cross-sectional study of US and Korean adults". The exploratory cross-sectional study compares muscle mass definitions and triglyceride-glucose-body mass index components in selected US NHANES 2005-2006, 2013-2014 and 2017-2018 and Korean KNHANES 2008-2011 analysis samples. SDC_2_Aggregate_results.zip contains aggregate model coefficients, confidence intervals, counts, diagnostics and figure source data. summary: Rank Access and Closure Depth in the Relation-Layer Cohomology of Token Arenas A refuted conjecture, a refuted mechanism, and two species of invariant harmonic residue     Driven by Dean Kulik October 2026     Abstract A K disj -type relation layer over a token arena assigns cohomology to a graph by declaring which closed loops count as relations. We settle an open problem about such layers and then identify what actually governs them. First, the conjecture that two vertex orbits force ε harm ( K 4 ) = 0 is refuted by an exact 12-vertex counterexample with |Aut| = 24, reproduced by two implementations whose constructions of the invariant cochain space share no logic. Second, we localize the failure: it is not a shortage of cells. On the witness's two-dimensional residue, all 1083 arena 4-cycles supply rank 1, while 20 arena 3-cycles of an excluded shape supply rank 2, and the two nonzero square families have the same image, a single line. Third, we refute the natural mechanism for this — that the residue is an odd-cycle blind spot — by exhibiting bipartite arenas, containing no odd cycle of any length, that still carry residue. The operative property is omission from the declared family, not parity. Fourth, we prove that ε harm ( K 3,4 ) > 0 on an infinite family — every cycle graph with n ≥ 5 and 2 ≤ K ≤ n−1, under the trivial group and the rotation subgroup, and zero under the full dihedral group — answering a question the odd-cycle reading had posed. Fifth, we define closure depth L closure , prove it exceeds 4 for every member of that family, and measure it as exactly n for C n and 4 for the witness, so no short vocabulary closes the family. This separates two populated regimes: residue a longer reader dissolves, and residue carried by configuration-space topology. Finally we identify the second kind. At trivial group the framework's own quantity is simplicial H 1 over ℚ , and the declared cells are the 2-skeleton of Abrams' discretized configuration space; the cell counts and Euler characteristic are verified against closed form, Abrams' subdivision hypothesis for C n reduces to n ≥ K + 1, the measured rank is 1 on all 33 admissible rows and 0 on all 8 excluded boundary rows, and the equivariant degree is solved exactly: +1 for rotations, −1 for reflections. All arithmetic is exact rational. Keywords: graph configuration space, graph braid group, token graph, discrete Morse theory, equivariant cohomology, cube complex, relation layer, closure depth MSC 2020: 55R80, 05C10, 20F36, 55N91, 05C85 License: CC BY-NC 4.0. Source code and executed notebook accompany this paper; see Appendix B. 1. Introduction A graph does not come with a cohomology. One is obtained by declaring a relation layer: a set of closed loops in some derived space that are stipulated to bound. Change the declaration and the cohomology changes while the graph does not. This paper is about what that dependence actually is, measured rather than described. The derived space here is a token arena . Fix a finite simple graph X , an integer K ≥ 1, and a group G ≤ Aut( X ). The arena A K ( X ) has the K -element subsets of V ( X ) as vertices, with an edge whenever two subsets differ by moving one token along one edge of X . A relation layer declares a family of arena loops as 2-cells; the G -invariant cochain complex of the resulting 2-complex has a first cohomology whose dimension we write ε harm . The quantity is relative to the declaration, and that is the point. Two declarations are natural and were already in use. K disj admits only commuting squares : two token moves along base edges with disjoint closed supports, which therefore commute. K 4 admits every 4-cycle of the arena. Since K disj ⊆ K 4 , monotonicity gives ε harm ( K 4 ) ≤ ε harm ( K disj ), and the interesting question is when the larger family closes what the smaller one l

summary: Rank Access and Closure Depth in the Relation-Layer Cohomology of Token Arenas A refuted conjecture, a refuted mechanism, and two species of invariant harmonic residue     Driven by Dean Kulik October 2026     Abstract A K disj -type relation layer over a token arena assigns cohomology to a graph by declaring which closed loops count as relations. We settle an open problem about such layers and then identify what actually governs them. First, the conjecture that two vertex orbits force ε harm ( K 4 ) = 0 is refuted by an exact 12-vertex counterexample with |Aut| = 24, reproduced by two implementations whose constructions of the invariant cochain space share no logic. Second, we localize the failure: it is not a shortage of cells. On the witness's two-dimensional residue, all 1083 arena 4-cycles supply rank 1, while 20 arena 3-cycles of an excluded shape supply rank 2, and the two nonzero square families have the same image, a single line. Third, we refute the natural mechanism for this — that the residue is an odd-cycle blind spot — by exhibiting bipartite arenas, containing no odd cycle of any length, that still carry residue. The operative property is omission from the declared family, not parity. Fourth, we prove that ε harm ( K 3,4 ) > 0 on an infinite family — every cycle graph with n ≥ 5 and 2 ≤ K ≤ n−1, under the trivial group and the rotation subgroup, and zero under the full dihedral group — answering a question the odd-cycle reading had posed. Fifth, we define closure depth L closure , prove it exceeds 4 for every member of that family, and measure it as exactly n for C n and 4 for the witness, so no short vocabulary closes the family. This separates two populated regimes: residue a longer reader dissolves, and residue carried by configuration-space topology. Finally we identify the second kind. At trivial group the framework's own quantity is simplicial H 1 over ℚ , and the declared cells are the 2-skeleton of Abrams' discretized configuration space; the cell counts and Euler characteristic are verified against closed form, Abrams' subdivision hypothesis for C n reduces to n ≥ K + 1, the measured rank is 1 on all 33 admissible rows and 0 on all 8 excluded boundary rows, and the equivariant degree is solved exactly: +1 for rotations, −1 for reflections. All arithmetic is exact rational. Keywords: graph configuration space, graph braid group, token graph, discrete Morse theory, equivariant cohomology, cube complex, relation layer, closure depth MSC 2020: 55R80, 05C10, 20F36, 55N91, 05C85 License: CC BY-NC 4.0. Source code and executed notebook accompany this paper; see Appendix B. 1. Introduction A graph does not come with a cohomology. One is obtained by declaring a relation layer: a set of closed loops in some derived space that are stipulated to bound. Change the declaration and the cohomology changes while the graph does not. This paper is about what that dependence actually is, measured rather than described. The derived space here is a token arena . Fix a finite simple graph X , an integer K ≥ 1, and a group G ≤ Aut( X ). The arena A K ( X ) has the K -element subsets of V ( X ) as vertices, with an edge whenever two subsets differ by moving one token along one edge of X . A relation layer declares a family of arena loops as 2-cells; the G -invariant cochain complex of the resulting 2-complex has a first cohomology whose dimension we write ε harm . The quantity is relative to the declaration, and that is the point. Two declarations are natural and were already in use. K disj admits only commuting squares : two token moves along base edges with disjoint closed supports, which therefore commute. K 4 admits every 4-cycle of the arena. Since K disj ⊆ K 4 , monotonicity gives ε harm ( K 4 ) ≤ ε harm ( K disj ), and the interesting question is when the larger family closes what the smaller one l

summary: Occupational heat exposure is an important health risk in construction, particularly in hot-arid climates where ambient heat, physical workload, protective clothing and restricted recovery interact. This pilot study developed a transparent Construction Heat and Hydration Risk Index (CHHRI) using de-identified environmental monitoring and administrative rotation records from a construction setting in Saudi Arabia. Quantitative analysis comprised a convenience pilot subset of 87 hourly heat-index observations from seven complete monitoring sheets. Heat index ranged from 31 to 55 (mean 46.6 ± 6.1); 74.7% of observations were in the operational Danger category and 17.2% in Extreme Danger. CHHRI integrates environmental heat severity, workload, PPE thermal burden, hydration deficit and recovery deficit on a 0–100 scale. Only the environmental component used observed quantitative data; the other four components were examined using 5,000 explicitly simulated, non-empirical scenarios. Baseline weights are provisional conceptual values, and alternative-weight sensitivity was evaluated. CHHRI is presented as a decision-support research prototype, not a validated predictor of heat illness.
title: Integrated Heat and Hydration Risk Framework for Construction Workers in Hot-Arid Environments

summary: Extended Classical Mechanics (ECM) describes the photon as an energetic physical entity whose interaction with an external gravitational field proceeds by direct force- and energy–momentum exchange, rather than through the geometric curvature of spacetime. This paper develops the ECM account of photon dynamics in external gravitational fields, with gravitational redshift interpreted as the expenditure of an acquired gravitational interaction-energy component Eɢ rather than as a depletion of the photon’s inherent frequency-defined energy. The photon’s inherent state is fixed by Eᵢₙₕₑᵣₑₙₜ = hf_photon = −Mᵃᵖᵖc², where Mᵃᵖᵖ < 0 is the Negative Apparent Mass (NAM) associated with the energetic reduction of the emitting electron. A coordinate framework for the photon–field interaction is constructed in which successive interaction stages generate external-field momentum displacements through Δpₑₓₜ = h/Δλ and its reverse-branch counterpart Δpₑₓₜ = h/(−Δλ), organised as a symmetric blueshift–redshift trajectory about the inherent reference state. The complete state-generation chain x° → f → Δf → λ → Δλ → Δpₑₓₜ → ΔG is established together with the ECM phase transformation Tₓˆ = x°/360°f = Δt, providing a rigorous, data-driven basis for graphing the exchange without arbitrary coordinates. An explicit nine-point displacement data set is specified, the complete coordinate table is computed, and the exchange trajectory is graphed.
title: Photon Dynamics in External Gravitational Fields: Energy–Momentum Exchange Between Photons and Gravitational Fields in Extended Classical Mechanics

summary: The application of machine learning to cryptocurrency price prediction requires a decisive pivot from uncalibrated point forecasting toward structural regime awareness. Standard higher-order central moments fail in cryptocurrency environments because polynomial exponentiation amplifies heavy-tailed noise precisely when stable detection is most critical. The Exact Linear Statistical Moments framework (M1, M2, M3, M4) solves this problem by tracking the true geometric deformation of phase space using robust order statistics. By establishing the Brownian benchmark E[M4] = 2.0, this framework identifies superdiffusive breakdown of restoring forces prior to systemic market crises. When integrated as a dynamic gating engine for multimodal deep learning models (SARIMAX, LSTM, AdaBoost-LSTMs), it resolves the divergence between statistical error metrics and real-world trading solvency, providing an early-warning and capital-preservation pipeline for digital asset markets.
title: Geometric Regime Shift Detection in Cryptocurrency Markets: Enhancing Multimodal Deep Learning with Exact Linear Statistical Moments

summary: Abstract   The Universal Research System with Reverse Itinerary (SUII) is a retrospective analytical methodology designed to reconstruct, in a traceable and auditable manner, the probable pathway leading from an initial problem or question to a completed scientific product. This manual brings together the universal prompt, a mandatory common core, ten core modules—including bibliographic analysis (SUII-B)—and six specialised extensions: journalistic and opinion texts (SUII-P), audiovisual or audio documents (SUII-AV), legislation and regulatory documents (SUII-L), case law and judicial decisions (SUII-J), critical appraisal of scientific articles (SUII-LC), and traceable research information management for datasets and research data objects (SUII-TRIM). Each module guides the extraction of locatable traces, classification of the epistemic status of claims, and construction of matrices linking evidence, inference, confidence, alternatives, and required verification. SUII-TRIM extends this logic to the provenance, versioning, transformation, quality control, preservation, access, and reuse of research datasets, while preserving the distinction between directly observed information, information provided by the researcher, reasoned inference, and non-determinable information. The method separates retrospective reconstruction from the prospective generation of hypotheses and requires rival explanations whenever the evidence does not support a unique conclusion. It also incorporates procedures for methodological auditing, version comparison, conceptual genealogy, peer review, algorithmic-bias assessment, external validation, teaching, and traceable research data management. SUII is not intended to recover the authors’ actual psychological history or to replace validated tools for methodological appraisal, risk-of-bias assessment, certainty of evidence, data stewardship, or repository curation. Its application requires version-controlled corpora, decision logs, retention of prompts and outputs, source verification, preservation of original data objects when applicable, and mandatory human oversight. When the available traces are insufficient, the appropriate result is “not determinable.” The manual provides practical criteria for selecting, combining, and quality-controlling the modules according to the product under analysis and the research objective, while maintaining explicit boundaries between documented evidence, reasoned inference, speculation, and unresolved uncertainty .   Resumen   El Sistema Universal de Investigación con Itinerario Inverso (SUII) es una metodología de análisis retrospectivo orientada a reconstruir, de forma trazable y auditable, el itinerario probable que conduce desde un problema o pregunta inicial hasta un producto científico finalizado. Este manual reúne el prompt universal, un núcleo común obligatorio, diez módulos nucleares y seis extensiones especializadas: análisis bibliográfico (SUII-B), textos periodísticos y de opinión (SUII-P), documentos audiovisuales o sonoros (SUII-AV), legislación y normativa (SUII-L), jurisprudencia y sentencias (SUII-J), lectura crítica de artículos científicos (SUII-LC) y gestión trazable de información y datos de investigación (SUII-TRIM). Cada módulo guía la extracción de huellas localizables, la clasificación del estado epistemológico de las afirmaciones y la construcción de matrices que relacionan evidencia, inferencia, confianza, alternativas y comprobaciones necesarias. El método separa la reconstrucción retrospectiva de la generación prospectiva de hipótesis y exige formular explicaciones rivales cuando la evidencia no permite una conclusión única. Asimismo, incorpora procedimientos para auditoría me

summary: Code and text-free reproducibility artifacts for the manuscript “Saudi Arabic Automatic Speech Recognition and Dialect Identification Using Calibrated System Combination and Gated Multimodal Fusion,” currently under revision at Scientific Reports . The repository implements a Saudi Arabic automatic speech recognition framework using XLSR-53, XLS-R 300M, XLS-R 1B, and MMS-1B with validation-tuned KenLM decoding, evaluation under a dialect-normalized scoring convention applied to both references and hypotheses, and calibrated N-best system combination. The reproduced combined test WER is 32.49% , compared with 34.04% for the best single-model configuration. XLSR-53 was evaluated on a 1,652-utterance subset of the test set and is therefore treated as an indicative baseline. The repository also provides SaudiDID-X, a multimodal Saudi dialect identification framework using frozen multi-layer MMS-1B acoustic representations and frozen SaudiBERT text features with a residual adapter and gated fusion. The audio-only comparison is the acoustic branch of the same SaudiDID-X training run , not an independently trained model. The archived test macro-F1 values are 52.01% for the audio-only branch and 53.79% for SaudiDID-X. The release includes analysis and reference-training notebooks, configuration metadata, anonymized split identifiers, text-free per-utterance result artifacts, statistical-test outputs, figures, tables, checksums, and a verification script. Raw audio and third-party transcriptions are not redistributed because of source-specific licensing restrictions. v1.0.2: Documentation, provenance, and configuration-metadata corrections. Archived predictions, primary reported metrics, data splits, checksums, and computational implementation are unchanged. See CHANGELOG.md for the complete list of corrections. v1.0.1: Configuration-metadata corrections for the single-run reporting protocol and per-stage training hyperparameters. No result values changed.

summary: GradLint is a fast, standalone Rust-based command-line tool and Python package for diffusion MRI gradient-table quality control. It audits FSL and MRtrix gradient schemes, detects b-vector flip and axis-permutation errors using DWI image evidence, and writes corrected gradient tables with machine-readable provenance. GradLint is designed as a QC gate before diffusion MRI preprocessing, reconstruction, or tractography pipelines. It checks whether the supplied gradient table is geometrically consistent with the diffusion image, reports scheme-quality issues such as shell structure, direction counts, b0 handling, non-unit b-vectors, and angular sampling, and identifies silent convention errors that can otherwise propagate into tensor fitting and tractography results. The core detection method ranks signed axis permutations of the gradient table by a fibre-coherence criterion derived from a diffusion tensor fit. Candidate conventions are evaluated in the appropriate image or world frame for the input format: FSL bvec/bval tables are treated as image-relative, while MRtrix .b tables are treated as world-coordinate gradients. When a high-confidence correction is found, GradLint can emit repaired FSL and/or MRtrix gradient files together with JSON provenance describing the decision, transform, inputs, and outputs.  The software is implemented as a Rust core with thin command-line and Python interfaces. The Python package exposes the same functionality as the CLI and can render JSON reports to Markdown or HTML. Input gradient files are never modified in place unless an explicit overwrite option is used. This record archives the source code for GradLint v1.1.6, corresponding to the GitHub release published on 2026-10-03. The archived source includes the Rust core, CLI, Python bindings, report rendering layer, tests, CI/release metadata, and example materials included in the public source tree. Repository: https://github.com/marcotag93/GradLint Release: https://github.com/marcotag93/GradLint/releases/tag/v1.1.6 PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/gradlint/ Concept DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20847595
title: GradLint: Fast gradient-scheme QC, b-vector flip detection, and repair for diffusion MRI

summary: Language functions not only as a means of transmitting information but also as a repository of cultural knowledge, collective experience, and culturally shaped patterns of thought. Consequently, translation involves more than the transfer of lexical and grammatical information between languages. It also requires the interpretation and reconstruction of meanings that are embedded within particular cultural contexts. This issue becomes especially evident in the translation of idioms, proverbs, metaphors, realia, and other culture-specific expressions whose meanings cannot always be derived from their individual lexical components. In Translation Studies, such elements are commonly discussed as culture-specific items (CSIs), which may require particular strategies to preserve their semantic, pragmatic, and cultural dimensions in the target language (Aixelá, 1996).
tags: Idiomatic expressions provide a particularly clear illustration of the relationship between language and culture.
title: AI TRANSLATION OF CULTURE-SPECIFIC AND IDIOMATIC EXPRESSIONS: LINGUISTIC AND CULTURAL CHALLENGES

summary: Sunnycode v1 provides an open-access computational framework and reproducibility package supporting the research article Failure-Aware Gateway Placement and Road-Constrained Backbone Optimization for Resilient Urban LoRaWAN Networks , submitted to Digital Communications and Networks. The framework integrates OpenStreetMap (OSM) building-level sensing demand, radio-frequency (RF) feasibility, capacity-aware gateway assignment, worst-case single-gateway failure retention (N−1), gateway-load fairness, and road-constrained Steiner backbone synthesis. The repository includes Python implementations of the proposed optimization approach and four independent benchmark methods (Genetic Algorithm, Particle Swarm Optimization, Greedy, and Random Search). Dataset and experimental scope The computational experiment considers 685 building-level sensor anchors, 169 road vertices, 195 street edges, and 89 gateway candidates. The Full benchmark comprises 4,000 run-level observations obtained from 100 repetitions for each combination of five optimization methods and eight gateway budgets (k = 3–10). Repository contents Python source code and computational validation utilities. Nine original CSV files containing experimental observations, aggregated statistics, evaluation effort, and optimizer provenance. OpenStreetMap territorial input ( sunny3.osm ). Forty scientific figures in PDF format. Installation and execution instructions using Anaconda. SHA-256 file-integrity manifest and licensing information. The archived results support independent verification of the reported statistics and new computational experiments. The original historical environment metadata and detailed event histories are not included; therefore, bit-for-bit replay of the historical execution environment is not claimed. Scientific scope: RF coverage and packet delivery ratio are model-derived planning estimates rather than field-calibrated measurements. N−1 resilience represents gateway-access service retention and does not certify fault-tolerant physical-backbone connectivity. This software and dataset are released to support transparent computational research, independent assessment, and further development of resilient urban Internet of Things infrastructure planning.
title: Sunnycode v1 A Reproducible Framework for Failure-Aware Gateway Placement and Road-Constrained Backbone Optimization in Urban LoRaWAN Networks

summary: Classical metaphysics treats the mutual exclusivity of alternatives as primitive: or, in its physical reading, excludes by nature. This paper argues the polarity should be reversed. Exclusivity is an achievement — stated, interior, structural content of the alternatives them-selves — rather than an intrinsic feature of disjunction; and once exclusion is relocated from the exterior of or to interior content, a new composition regime falls out with no further postulation: the joint regime, in which co-present alternatives simply decline to carry mu-tual negations. The difference between the regimes is fixed by a one-statement test, which answers the suspicion of mere notation; a strict fence separates what the new primitive sup-plies (openness) from anything its occupants might do with it (use), which blocks the two natural misreadings; and the primitive itself receives a deflationary definition: or-jointness is the logic-valued regime of not stating mutual negations on the interior side — obtained by declension, not addition. We argue the proposal reclassifies the color-exclusion problem that fractured the Tractatus, and supplies the determinable-based literature on metaphysical indeterminacy with the composition story it has lacked. A documented fact about the direction of discovery then bears on the proposal’s status: the two composition forms were first extracted, in companion work, from the case-by-case structure of interference phenomena — before the present philosophy existed — so the dichotomy’s shape is explained by what it was extracted from, not by any philosophical purpose it might serve. Whether the world instantiates the joint regime is the companion framework’s proposal, on which no thesis here leans; what the provenance establishes is that the primitive was not gerrymandered for the argument that now exposes it.
title: Exclusivity as Achievement: Relocating Mutual Exclusion to the Interior, and the Logical Primitive That Falls Out

summary: Abstract We present a comprehensive, universal, abstract group-theoretic, module-theoretic, and category-theoretic formalization of bijectively separated rank arithmetic . Given an arbitrary family of algebraic groups {Gi}r i=1 and elements Pi ∈ Gi with finite multiplicative orders oi = ord(Pi), we establish that the additive rank-coordinate space A(P) = Qri=1 Z/oiZ is canonically isomorphic to the external direct product of cyclic power orbits G(P) = Qri=1⟨Pi⟩ under the coordinate evaluation map ΦP(([ni]oi)i) = (Pnii)i. We prove that coordinatewise multiplication in the multiplicative state space corresponds strictly to coordinatewise addition of discrete expo- nent rank classes without introducing analytic logarithms, continuous curves, branch cuts, or topological ambiguities. We extend this framework to general category- theoretic limits, establishing that sub-space coordinate projections and factor permutation reindexings form natural transformations in the category of groups Grp. Furthermore, when lane outputs collapse into a single target background group H, we isolate the exact relation subgroup KP =ker(ΨP) and prove the quotient isomorphism A(P)/KP∼= ⟨P1, . . . , Pr⟩ ≤ H, measuring the precise algebraic information lost during scalar collapse. Finally, we formulate the extension to infinite complex power orbits , polynomial root reconstruction via Newton symmetrization of ranked power arrays Pr ∈ Cr×r, Chinese Remainder Theorem grid decompositions over composite moduli, native linear rank complexity bounds Θ(m), and an axiomatic minimal proof assistant kernel . Keywords: Abstract algebra, cyclic groups, direct products, exponent coordinates, re- lation lattices, projection functors, natural transformations, Newton identities, Chinese Remainder Theorem, rank complexity. summary: This dataset supports the study “A methodological evaluation of deposited-assembly usability and raw-read rescue in a global public Klebsiella pneumoniae genome collection.” It contains accession-level manifests, derived statistical tables, figure-source data, documentation, software-version information, and analysis code supporting an assembly-first workflow with raw-read reconstruction for publicly available sequencing records. Starting from 44,278 geographically resolved eligible records, 1,687 records had no analyzable public genome input, leaving 42,591 records with an analyzable genome input. Of these, two were excluded during final cohort harmonization, resulting in a final analytical collection of 42,589 K. pneumoniae genomes. summary: This chapter develops the research programme of Generative Relational Economics (GRE) by translating the conceptual, methodological, and substantive architectures developed earlier in the book into a cumulative, contestable, and revisable programme of inquiry. Its principal concern is answerability: GRE claims should specify what is being investigated, what kinds of evidence can support them, what would count against them, which methods are appropriate to their objects, and under what conditions their scope, formulation, or status should change. The chapter first distinguishes the epistemic status of GRE claims and establishes a modular research architecture. It then formulates research programmes for relational economic structures, allocation, heterogeneous value, value conversion and circulation, generative return, generative spacetime, fast–slow dynamics, economic power, justice, generative exploitation, epistemic economy, and AI-mediated capability asymmetry. These substantive programmes are complemented by domain studies, formal modelling, historical and interpretive inquiry, quantitative and empirical research, comparative theory, institutional experimentation, measurement analysis, counterevidence, negative results, replication, reinterpretation, and research infrastructure. A recurring concern is to prevent operationalization from collapsing the distinctions that motivate GRE. Measurement is therefore treated as a transformation with possible loss and reflexive effects; formalization is treated as task-relative rather than as evidence of ontological commitment; justice research keeps normative premises explicit; power and exploitation require mechanism-level identification rather than inference from asymmetry alone; and cross-domain translation preserves non-equivalence and domain-specific remainders. Failed models, failed translations, null results, counterexamples, and negative evidence are treated as constitutive resources for cumulative research rather than as residuals to be discarded. The chapter concludes by specifying how GRE may interact with neighboring Generative Relational domains while retaining disciplinary containment. Candidate cross-domain structures remain hypotheses for further inquiry rather than presumptive components of a completed general theory. GRE thereby emerges not as a closed theoretical system, but as an open research programme whose concepts, methods, models, and domain claims remain historically situated, empirically answerable, formally inspectable, and institutionally revisable.
title: Generative Relational Economics - Chapter 22: Research Programme of Generative Relational Economics

summary: Complete data, code and manuscript for the preprint of the same title. Contains the AlphaFold3 predictions, derived per-sample tables, measured kinetics, analysis code and a self-checking reproduce.py that regenerates every number reported in the paper using the Python standard library alone. Two results. (1) Across 18 non-cognate amino acids, none of three AlphaFold3 confidence observables tracks the published substrate discrimination factors of threonyl-tRNA synthetase (Spearman rho = -0.010, +0.098, -0.028; all p > 0.56); serine, the non-cognate this enzyme rejects best at the binding step, scores highest of all 18 on every observable. (2) The same scores are not blind to the structure: substituting the three zinc-binding residues with alanine collapses the threonine-over-valine preference by 0.112 (95% CI 0.106-0.117) and inverts it, without changing the predicted fold. Combined: the readout is site-sensitive but not affinity-calibrated. Measured discrimination factors are transcribed with attribution from Freist, Sternbach & Cramer (1994) Eur J Biochem 220:745-752, doi:10.1111/j.1432-1033.1994.tb18675.x.
title: Structure-prediction confidence detects an enzyme's catalytic site but does not measure how well it discriminates: data, code and manuscript

summary: The DSM-861 establishes a deterministic computing architecture realized in standard CMOS digital logic. By organizing the physical Network-on-Chip along the distance-transitive Johnson association scheme J(42, 2), the design enforces an invariant network diameter of D = 2 and enables single-cycle static routing across 34,440 dedicated channels, eliminating dynamic arbitration queues and buffers. By replacing classical matrix multiplications with 4-stage pipelined Chebyshev polynomial edge engines, the architecture realizes the Kolmogorov–Arnold network decomposition in fixedpoint Q1.14 arithmetic. Roundoff drift is mitigated at the node level by projecting activations onto the maximal class-number-one algebraic integer ring O−163 using an exact 4-point Euclidean minimum-distance snapping unit, while non-admissible phases are intercepted by a 72-sector modular sieve and flushed to a null register on every clock cycle. Recursive allocation is bounded by Euler’s conductor prime m = 41 via colexicographical address folding, enforcing an invariant replication ceiling on silicon. The result is a self-contained, mathematically closed processing architecture that provides high compute density, bounded memory footprints, and deterministic execution for artificial intelligence hardware.
title: A Wholly Digital KAN-DAM Processor via Exact Chebyshev Polynomial Engines, Distance-Transitive Johnson Interconnects, and Algebraic Lattice Snapping

summary: Occupational heat exposure is an important health risk in construction, particularly in hot-arid climates where ambient heat, physical workload, protective clothing and restricted recovery interact. This pilot study developed a transparent Construction Heat and Hydration Risk Index (CHHRI) using de-identified environmental monitoring and administrative rotation records from a construction setting in Saudi Arabia. Quantitative analysis comprised a convenience pilot subset of 87 hourly heat-index observations from seven complete monitoring sheets. Heat index ranged from 31 to 55 (mean 46.6 ± 6.1); 74.7% of observations were in the operational Danger category and 17.2% in Extreme Danger. CHHRI integrates environmental heat severity, workload, PPE thermal burden, hydration deficit and recovery deficit on a 0–100 scale. Only the environmental component used observed quantitative data; the other four components were examined using 5,000 explicitly simulated, non-empirical scenarios. Baseline weights are provisional conceptual values, and alternative-weight sensitivity was evaluated. CHHRI is presented as a decision-support research prototype, not a validated predictor of heat illness.
title: Integrated Heat and Hydration Risk Framework for Construction Workers in Hot-Arid Environments

summary: CORE-LLM-Bench is a controlled neurosymbolic benchmark for evaluating ontology-grounded reasoning in large language models. Version 1.1.0 contains 9,048 unique question-hop instances derived from four ontology datasets: Family, Pizza 100, Pizza 250, and OWL2Bench. The benchmark contains 6,032 binary question-answering (BQA) instances and 3,016 open-ended question-answering (OEQA) instances. Benchmark instances support 1-hop and 2-hop ontology contexts and aligned natural-language (NL), formal-symbolic (FS), and entity-abstracted (AR) representations. Ground-truth answers and explanation structures are derived using symbolic ontology reasoning, enabling controlled evaluation according to task formulation, representation, semantic abstraction, context depth, explanation-based reasoning complexity, and reasoning type. The release includes benchmark data, reasoning metadata, provenance and licensing documentation, release manifests and checksums, and scripts supporting benchmark generation, validation, Hugging Face export, and reproducibility. The canonical source-code release is CORE-LLM-Bench v1.1.0 on GitHub. Licensing is component-specific. summary: This repository provides the code, fitted probe weights, steering vectors, and experimental records for SelfHalt: Auditing Activation Steering for LLM Reasoning-Length Control . The archive includes experiment and analysis scripts, 85 probe/vector files, raw experimental outputs, frozen configurations, statistical reports, and CPU-only verification tools. It preserves positive, negative, and inconclusive findings, including positional-confounding controls and comparisons with alternative length-control strategies. The work distinguishes prediction of generation termination from semantic reasoning completion: a decodable near-end signal or a reduction in output length does not, by itself, establish that reasoning is complete. No manuscript, paper figures, or foundation-model weights are included. Some experiments require separately obtained models and upstream dependencies. The bundled numerical replays verify saved evidence within their documented scope; they do not reproduce every model-generation experiment. Author software is provided under the MIT License. Experimental records follow the included CC BY 4.0 rights notice, with third-party licenses and attributions preserved. See README.md and WEIGHTS_GUIDE.md for usage, provenance, and limitations.

summary: This dataset completes the report of the same author (Olivier Brunner) that can be viewed at : https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.15696776 It is composed of three consistant CSV files -  i.e. with the same columns. The v12 report abstract is : This report presents solutions that, as of the date of publication, improve the cost (makespan) for 57 instances of the Permutation Flow-Shop Problem (PFSP) proposed by Eric Taillard or by Eva Vallada, Rubén Ruiz, and Jose M. Framinan. This report may help those who assess the quality of heuristics based on their ability to approach the best-known solutions. Three algorithmic techniques used are also presented: the super-prohibition sieve excluding paths with weights exceeding a given bound, the adaptive compartmental neighborhood with selective 2-closing, and finally the makespan calculation performed using upper-windowed multi-numbers. The same versioning is used for the report and for the dataset. The dataset was created and starts at version 5 of the report. Sources 100, 101 & 102 : The results of an ongoing work of the author. Further updates will be posted until every open instance has been tested. Source 0 : The best known solutions sumerized and uploaded by Jan Gmys in feb, 2021. It can be viewed at : https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.4542886 Source 50 (including v4 and previous versions; the best solutions are not always in the latest version): The solutions uploaded by J. A. Alejandro-Soto. v4 can be viewed at : https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.15832204 The "Optimal" column in each CSV is now renamed "OptimalityNotRefuted" and sh ould be interpreted with caution.
title: Permutation Flow-shop : Taillard and VFR benchmarks best known solutions (updated according to linked report)

summary: Greenhouse climate control is a complex problem due to its nonlinear dynamic and the influence of strong external disturbances. This work proposes a control strategy based on Reinforcement Learning (RL) trained in offline mode to regulate the temperature of a Mediterranean greenhouse through natural ventilation. To this end, the Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) algorithm is employed, trained using experience collected from a real system under the operation of a proportional-integral controller (PI) considered as an expert system. The resulting policies are evaluated using data not used for learning. The results show that the agent accurately replicates the behavior of the expert controller, generating smooth control signals consistent with the system dynamics, with a control effort reduction of 7.4 % compared to the PI. This work is limited to the offline training and validation of the agent using real process data, without considering its direct deployment on the plant at this stage.
title: Offline Reinforcement Learning for Greenhouse Temperature Control through Natural Ventilation

This work proposes a control strategy based on Reinforcement Learning (RL) trained in offline mode to regulate the temperature of a Mediterranean greenhouse through natural ventilation. To this end, the Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) algorithm is employed, trained using experience collected from a real system under the operation of a proportional-integral controller (PI) considered as an expert system. The resulting policies are evaluated using data not used for learning. The results show that the agent accurately replicates the behavior of the expert controller, generating smooth control signals consistent with the system dynamics, with a control effort reduction of 7.4 % compared to the PI. This work is limited to the offline training and validation of the agent using real process data, without considering its direct deployment on the plant at this stage.

summary: Independent replication of the claim that the 30 m random-forest model of natural forest regeneration of Williams et al. (2024, Nature) has 87.9 % validation accuracy, tested in Colombia with open data and new code. Verdict: partially supported. The accuracy reproduces under random validation (0.887) but is lower under spatially blocked validation (0.812-0.869), for a model trained outside Colombia (0.767), and when predicting 2012-2024 regrowth from 2000-2012 with independent MapBiomas labels (0.717). The protocol follows the robustness checks suggested in The Unjournal's evaluation of the paper.
title: natural-regeneration-replication: testing the 87.9 % accuracy claim of Williams et al. (2024) in Colombia

summary: This repository contains the machine-learning surrogate pipeline for predicting size-resolved aerosol particle number concentrations (nucleation, Aitken, and accumulation modes) from conventional atmospheric variables over Beijing. The pipeline implements a two-stage stacked ensemble: a CatBoost classifier that stratifies samples into low/high-concentration regimes, three base regressors (XGBoost, Random Forest, RBF-SVR) per regime, and a LightGBM meta-learner that stacks base-learner predictions with 26 raw predictors. Pre-trained weights for all three particle modes are included, along with the held-out test set and scripts to reproduce the reported R2 and Pearson correlation metrics. The target variable is transformed with Yeo-Johnson standardization; predictions are written in the transformed space, and the provided power transformer allows inverse transformation to physical units (cm-3).
title: Learning size-resolved aerosol number concentrations from conventional atmospheric variables: insights from Beijing

summary: Reproducibility package for the manuscript "Which evidence does the rule require? A page-anchored comparison of a Philippine rabies category-II exemption across two guideline versions." The package contains the frozen rule catalogue and migration specification extracted from DOH Administrative Order 2018-0013 and the document labeled AO 2026-0010; the synthetic boundary-case corpus and the case-eligibility audit; the seeded-defect mutation manifest; the comparator result tables and the plot-data behind every figure; the three manuscript figures as vector PDF, editable SVG and 600 dpi PNG; the provenance ledger recording source hashes and the ambiguities that remain unresolved; and the analysis implementation with its test suite. Every rule statement is anchored to a verified page of the original PDF. The source documents themselves are the property of their issuers and are NOT redistributed; the deposit records their SHA-256 digests so a reader who obtains them from the issuer can reproduce every quoted span. This is research software. It is not clinical decision support, it returns no treatment recommendation, and no patient data of any kind is included. The reported figures are counts on a fixed synthetic corpus, not estimates of clinical sensitivity or specificity.
title: Source-to-rule verification of a Philippine rabies guideline migration: data, specifications, figures and analysis code

summary: CORE-LLM-Bench is a controlled neurosymbolic benchmark for evaluating ontology-grounded reasoning in large language models. Version 1.1.0 contains 9,048 unique question-hop instances derived from four ontology datasets: Family, Pizza 100, Pizza 250, and OWL2Bench. The benchmark contains 6,032 binary question-answering (BQA) instances and 3,016 open-ended question-answering (OEQA) instances. Benchmark instances support 1-hop and 2-hop ontology contexts and aligned natural-language (NL), formal-symbolic (FS), and entity-abstracted (AR) representations. Ground-truth answers and explanation structures are derived using symbolic ontology reasoning, enabling controlled evaluation according to task formulation, representation, semantic abstraction, context depth, explanation-based reasoning complexity, and reasoning type. The release includes benchmark data, reasoning metadata, provenance and licensing documentation, release manifests and checksums, and scripts supporting benchmark generation, validation, Hugging Face export, and reproducibility. The canonical source-code release is CORE-LLM-Bench v1.1.0 on GitHub. Licensing is component-specific. Repository software is MIT licensed; separable original CORE-LLM-Bench benchmark content is CC BY 4.0; Pizza-derived material follows CC BY 3.0; OWL2Bench-derived material follows Apache-2.0; and Family/FHKB-derived material follows CC BY-SA 3.0. See NOTICE.md for detailed provenance, attribution, and modification information.
title: CORE-LLM-Bench: A Controlled Neurosymbolic Benchmark for Ontology-Grounded Reasoning in Large Language Models

summary: This repository provides the code, fitted probe weights, steering vectors, and experimental records for SelfHalt: Auditing Activation Steering for LLM Reasoning-Length Control . The archive includes experiment and analysis scripts, 85 probe/vector files, raw experimental outputs, frozen configurations, statistical reports, and CPU-only verification tools. It preserves positive, negative, and inconclusive findings, including positional-confounding controls and comparisons with alternative length-control strategies. The work distinguishes prediction of generation termination from semantic reasoning completion: a decodable near-end signal or a reduction in output length does not, by itself, establish that reasoning is complete. No manuscript, paper figures, or foundation-model weights are included. Some experiments require separately obtained models and upstream dependencies. The bundled numerical replays verify saved evidence within their documented scope; they do not reproduce every model-generation experiment. Author software is provided under the MIT License. Experimental records follow the included CC BY 4.0 rights notice, with third-party licenses and attributions preserved. See README.md and WEIGHTS_GUIDE.md for usage, provenance, and limitations.
title: SelfHalt: Auditing Activation Steering for LLM Reasoning-Length Control

summary: Data accompanying N. Vauquier, B. M. L. Srivastava, S. A. Hosseini and E. Vincent, "Legally validated evaluation framework for voice anonymization", Interspeech 2025, pages 3229 to 3233, doi:10.21437/Interspeech.2025-1699. The paper introduces two metrics, Singling Out and Linkability, that translate the singling out and linkability criteria of the Article 29 Working Party's Opinion 05/2014 on Anonymization Techniques into quantities that can be measured on speech. The framework was formally validated by the French Data Protection Authority (CNIL). This record holds the data needed to reproduce the paper's results. The reference implementation is at https://github.com/brijmohan/voice-anonymization-legal-eval CONTENTS Dataset definitions, unchanged from version 1.0.0: cv11-A-filelist (19.5 MB): the Mozilla Common Voice 11.0 clips forming subset A, 22,024 speakers with at least 2 minutes of speech each. cv11-B-filelist (83.3 MB): the clips forming subset B, 4,949 speakers with at least 3 minutes each. Subset B's speakers are a subset of A's, with disjoint utterances. Cosine score matrices, new in version 2.0.0, 12 files totalling 5.2 GB: scores_<attacker>_L<length>.npy: a 22,024 x 4,949 float32 array per attacker model and conversation length. Entry [i, j] is the cosine similarity between enrollment speaker i of subset A and test speaker j of subset B. scores_<attacker>_L<length>.npy.json: a sidecar per matrix giving the row and column speaker order, so each matrix is self describing. MANIFEST.json: SHA-256 checksums and shapes for every file. The four attacker models differ in what their speaker embedding extractor was trained on: original : original speech, evaluated on original speech. ignorant : original speech. semi_informed : speech anonymized with VoicePrivacy 2022 baseline B1.a. informed : speech anonymized with VoicePrivacy 2024 baseline B1. Conversation length L is the number of utterances averaged per speaker, and takes the values 1, 3 and 30. Test data for the three attackers is anonymized with VoicePrivacy 2024 baseline B1. USING THE MATRICES pip install git+https://github.com/brijmohan/voice-anonymization-legal-eval from legal_eval.io import load_score_matrix from legal_eval.sweeps import linkability_sweep m = load_score_matrix("scores_informed_L1.npy") print(linkability_sweep(m, speaker_counts=[20, 100, 1000, 10000]).mean()) To check a download against the published results: python examples/03_verify_against_score_matrices.py --release-dir . That recomputes all 2,640 published Linkability points. Expect a worst case difference of about 0.005, which is Monte Carlo noise from averaging five runs. WHAT THE MATRICES CONTAIN These are similarity scores rather than speaker embeddings, but the distinction is smaller than it sounds and it is worth being explicit. Each matrix is the product of two sets of unit norm x-vectors, so its rank is bounded by the embedding dimension rather than by its shape. Measured on a random 3,000 x 3,000 block, the singular value spectrum collapses by four orders of magnitude immediately after index 256, which is the x-vector dimension, and a rank 256 reconstruction reproduces the released scores to within 2e-07. A recipient can therefore recover similarity structure that was never released, link a speaker across the four released conditions, and cluster speakers by voice similarity. ON THE SPEAKER LABELS Row and column labels are internal pseudonyms of the form spk-f-20851, not Mozilla Common Voice client identifiers. They should not be relied on as a safeguard. The subset file lists in this record are public, Common Voice publishes a client identifier for every clip, and the evaluation pipeline is openly reproducible, so a determined party could recompute an original condition matrix and align it to the released one to recover the mapping. The pseudonyms raise the cost of doing so. They do not prevent it. This release is published becaus

summary: Replication package for the systematic literature review "Production-Oriented Evaluation and Testing of LLM-Based Agents: A Systematic Literature Review" (revised version, submitted to Information and Software Technology; first submitted as "Evaluation and Testing of LLM-Based Agents in Production: A Systematic Literature Review"). The review follows Kitchenham–Charters guidelines with PRISMA 2020 reporting. The main search covers Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore and the ACM Digital Library up to 24 March 2026; with citation tracking it yields a review corpus of 88 primary studies (74 from the main search, 14 from citation tracking). A search extension to 25 September 2026 with the same query and criteria yields 314 further studies, reported as a separate update analysis. A Scopus sensitivity search with broader production-oriented terms (300-record random sample) estimates the recall of the query. Version 2.0.0 accompanies the revised article. Version 1.0.0 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20583928) accompanies the article as first submitted and is preserved unchanged in the folder 2026-03/. Contents: corpus/, extraction/, risk-of-bias/ — the review corpus of 88: included and excluded studies with screening decisions, dual data extraction (Reviewer 1, Reviewer 2 and arbiter-resolved; 27 analytical fields) and three-domain quality assessment. 2026-03/ — the March 2026 round exactly as released in v1.0.0 (80 studies, agreement reports, audits). 2026-09/ — the September 2026 round: ACM Digital Library and update searches (full-text records R001–R670), Scopus sensitivity search, extraction and quality assessment of 335 studies, agreement reports, and the single-label recode of automated-testing with its held-out validation. primary-studies.bib (88) and 2026-09/primary-studies.bib (335). reproduce.ipynb — a self-contained notebook with 595 automated checks that reproduce every statistic of the article computed from the per-record data (Section 2: review corpus; Section 3: September round; Appendix A: the 2026-03 round as first submitted). README.md (structure, data dictionary, errata), CHANGELOG.md, methodology.md, statistical-analyses.md, prisma-2020-checklist.md, kitchenham-2007-compliance.md, requirements.txt, LICENSE. To reproduce: install the dependencies (pip install -r requirements.txt) and run reproduce.ipynb top to bottom. Expected output: 595 checks passed, 0 failed. Licensed under CC BY 4.0.

summary: # Comprehensive Cross-Regional Cost Matrix and Industrial Scaling Dataset for Polymer-Based Static Pre-Mixers in Affordable Housing Retrofits **Associated Manuscript:** "Integrated computational design assessment of a compact crescent-vane pre-mixer for low-cost residential solar water heating"   **Target Journal:** Journal of Building Engineering (Elsevier)   **Geographical Scope:** Federative Republic of Brazil (All 5 Geopolitical Regions)   **Data Format:** Markdown Documentation, Structured Tables, and Integrated JSON Schema   --- ## 1. Dataset Overview and Rational Statement This dataset contains the empirical cross-regional retail market prices, industrial equipment asset costs, and taxed electricity utility rates used to compile the techno-economic feasibility framework in the associated research article.  Evaluating the scalability of additively manufactured (AM) components within the affordable housing sector (Habitações de Interesse Social - HIS) requires a geographically diverse baseline. Because Brazil is a country of continental dimensions heavily reliant on road freight transportation, industrial supply chains exhibit high regional price elasticity. Manufacturing hubs are primarily centralized within the South and Southeast states, imposing significant logistical overheads (e.g., interstate tax variations like the DIFAL-ICMS and fuel freight surcharges) on the peripheral North, Northeast, and Central-West regions. This open-access dataset ensures full methodological transparency and allows international reviewers and researchers to replicate the cost-benefit analysis. --- ## 2. Hardware and Material Production Constraints Processing engineering-grade Acrylonitrile Styrene Acrylate (ASA) under industrial manufacturing throughputs imposes strict technical constraints on the hardware architecture: 1. **Thermal Retention:** The machine must possess a fully sealed cabinet (closed enclosure) to retain internal thermal energy, preventing volumetric contraction, warping, and interlayer delamination. 2. **Volatile Filtration:** Because the thermal decomposition of molten ASA releases volatile organic compounds (VOCs)—specifically toxic styrene monomer vapors—the manufacturing enclosure must integrate an active filtration loop equipped with Activated Carbon (AC) blocks. --- ## 3. Data Matrices ### Matrix A: Cross-Regional Hydraulic Retail Price Matrix (Values in BRL) The following data tracks empirical retail prices from dominant building material distributors across the five geopolitical zones of Brazil, tracking traditional metal monocomandos and registros. The data confirms that traditional single-lever machined brass mixers are cost-prohibitive for affordable housing, maintaining a pondered national mean of BRL 644.00—approximately 41% of a minimum wage. | Geopolitical Region | Reference Outlets Audited | Monocomando | Dual-Control | Single Valve | | :--- | :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | | **Southeast** | Leroy Merlin, Telhanorte, Casa Mimosa | 645.00 | 320.00 | 85.00 | | **South** | Cassol Centerlar, Balaroti | 610.00 | 295.00 | 79.00 | | **Central-West** | AC Coelho, Sertão Materiais | 690.00 | 345.00 | 92.00 | | **Northeast** | Ferreira Costa, Carajás | 660.00 | 310.00 | 88.00 | | **North** | Nazaré Materiais, Bemol Lar | 715.00 | 360.00 | 98.00 | | **NATIONAL MEAN** | **Pondered Baseline Index** | **644.00** | **326.00** | **88.40** | ### Matrix B: Cross-Regional Industrial Asset and Raw Material Cost The following data tracks the localized retail acquisition cost for three commercial CoreXY FDM platforms satisfying the closed cabinet and AC filtration constraints, alongside the retail price per kilogram of engineering-grade ASA filament (1 kg spools). Prices were audited from official national distributors (e.g., 3D Prime) as of October 2026. | Geopolitical Region | Bambu Lab H2S (BRL) | Qidi Tech X-Max 3 (BRL) | Creality K1 Max (BRL) |

summary: Abstract. This article proposes quantified measures to strengthen sustainable financing mechanisms in Uzbekistan through financing instruments, pilot projects and phased reforms. It estimates renewable-energy and grid-modernization investment needs at USD 10.1 billion for 2026–2030 and argues that stronger domestic financing mechanisms are essential to reduce currency risk and dependence on external capital. Two pilot instruments are developed: regional green bonds and sustainability-linked bonds for state-owned enterprises, supported by sector-specific performance indicators. A three-scenario forecast projects cumulative green, social, sustainability and sustainability-linked bond issuance of USD 3.25–13.3 billion, with the domestic market’s share increasing from approximately 14 to 37 percent. Sensitivity analysis identifies domestic-market development and banks’ international issuance growth as the principal drivers. Under the baseline scenario, subsidizing coupons on half of domestic issuance would cost approximately USD 54 million, alongside USD 4.7 billion in additional issuance relative to the inertial scenario. The article also proposes transition finance, sustainable sukuk, carbon-market mechanisms, digital instruments and blended finance, sequenced over 2026–2035 and supported by a formal risk assessment. Key words: sustainable financing mechanisms, capital needs, municipal green bonds, sustainability-linked bonds, scenario forecasting, sensitivity analysis, coupon subsidy, transition finance, Uzbekistan. Annotatsiya. Ushbu maqolada moliyaviy vositalar, pilot loyihalar va bosqichma-bosqich islohotlar asosida O‘zbekistonda barqaror moliyalashtirish mexanizmlarini mustahkamlashga qaratilgan miqdoriy asoslangan chora-tadbirlar taklif etilgan. Tadqiqotda 2026–2030-yillarda qayta tiklanuvchi energetika va elektr tarmoqlarini modernizatsiya qilish uchun zarur investitsiyalar hajmi 10,1 mlrd AQSh dollari miqdorida baholangan hamda valyuta xatarlarini va tashqi kapitalga qaramlikni kamaytirish uchun ichki moliyalashtirish mexanizmlarini rivojlantirish zarurligi asoslab berilgan. Ikki turdagi pilot moliyaviy vosita — hududiy yashil obligatsiyalar hamda davlat korxonalari uchun barqarorlik ko‘rsatkichlariga bog‘langan obligatsiyalar ishlab chiqilgan bo‘lib, ular tarmoq xususiyatlariga mos samaradorlik ko‘rsatkichlari bilan qo‘llab-quvvatlanadi. Uchta ssenariy asosidagi prognozga ko‘ra, yashil, ijtimoiy, barqarorlik va barqarorlik ko‘rsatkichlariga bog‘langan obligatsiyalarning jami emissiyasi 3,25 mlrd AQSh dollaridan 13,3 mlrd AQSh dollarigacha yetishi, ichki bozor ulushi esa taxminan 14 foizdan 37 foizgacha oshishi mumkin. Sezgirlik tahlili ichki bozorning rivojlanishi va banklarning xalqaro obligatsiyalar emissiyasi o‘sishini asosiy ta’sir etuvchi omillar sifatida aniqlaydi. Bazaviy ssenariy bo‘yicha ichki emissiyaning yarmi uchun kupon to‘lovlarini subsidiyalash xarajatlari taxminan 54 mln AQSh dollarini tashkil etishi, shu bilan birga inertsiya ssenariysiga nisbatan qo‘shimcha emissiya hajmi 4,7 mlrd AQSh dollariga yetishi mumkin. Maqolada, shuningdek, o‘tish davri moliyasi, barqaror sukuk, uglerod bozori mexanizmlari, raqamli moliyaviy vositalar va aralash moliyalashtirish mexanizmlarini 2026–2035-yillarda bosqichma-bosqich joriy etish hamda ularni rasmiy risklarni baholash tizimi bilan qo‘llab-quvvatlash taklif etilgan. Kalit so‘zlar: barqaror moliyalashtirish mexanizmlari, kapitalga ehtiyoj, munitsipal yashil obligatsiyalar, barqarorlik ko‘rsatkichlariga bog‘langan obligatsiyalar, ssenariy asosida prognozlash, sezgirlik tahlili, kupon subsidiyasi, o‘tish davri moliyasi, O‘zbekiston. summary: Accurate attitude estimation is a fundamental requirement for achieving stable flight and reliable control of quadrotor unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). However, failures or abnormal measurements of the Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU) may interrupt attitude feedback and severely degrade flight performance. This paper proposes a Virtual IMU Sensor (VIMUS) based on a Nonlinear AutoRegressive network with eXogenous inputs (NARX) to estimate roll and pitch angles from control inputs and quadrotor dynamics. To evaluate its effectiveness, a Multilayer Perceptron (MLP)-based virtual sensor is implemented as a benchmark under identical training conditions. An IMU fault detection and switching mechanism is further integrated to automatically replace the original IMU with the proposed VIMUS when sensor faults occur. Simulation results show that the NARX-based VIMUS outperforms the MLP model, reducing the root mean square error (RMSE) by 62.3% and 64.6% for roll and pitch estimation, respectively, while achieving coefficients of determination (R²) of 0.986 and 0.991. The proposed framework enables continuous attitude feedback and provides an accurate and robust fault-tolerant solution for quadrotor attitude estimation and control.

summary: Reference implementation, evaluation harness, 20 hand-verified golden labels, the 26-document replication corpus manifest, raw run outputs of two campaigns, analysis scripts and two human-study instruments, supporting the manuscript "Source Grounding Verifies Retrieval and Not Interpretation in Automated Extraction from Construction Tender Documents". The workflow requires every surfaced value to be locatable in the source text before it is shown. This release adds the September 2026 campaign (C-R2-4DOC): 200 document-runs across six arms, archiving every field of every document of every run with the request outcome, latency and token usage of each call, so that every reported figure can be recomputed without querying the model. The deployed web application is deliberately excluded; it forms no part of the reported method.

summary: This poster presents a lunar surface simulation framework and synthetic dataset for evaluating visual-domain zero-shot sim-to-real transfer in lunar perception. The framework integrates terrain reconstruction, lunar surface appearance modelling, realistic illumination, and synthetic data generation to support controlled evaluation of visual fidelity and cross-dataset segmentation performance. Experimental results show that the proposed dataset achieves lower feature-space distance to real lunar imagery and stronger zero-shot segmentation performance across multiple model architectures. The work further investigates mixed-training strategies and key simulation design factors. Presented at the Towards Sustainability and Resiliency of Field Robotics Workshop, IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS 2025), Hangzhou, China, 20 October 2025. Honourable Mention for Best Poster Award.
title: A Novel Lunar Surface Simulation Framework Enabling Visual Domain Zero-Shot Sim-to-Real Transfer

summary: Replication package for the journal article on attributing LLM-paraphrased source code to the model that produced it, in the setting where someone has an LLM rewrite code that another person wrote so that it no longer looks copied. Contents: the corpus of 144,958 paraphrase pairs (22,053 human-written files in Python, C, C++, Java, C#, Go and PHP, rewritten by Gemini 3 Flash, GPT 5 Nano, Claude 3 Haiku, Qwen 3 Coder 30B, DeepSeek V3.2, Grok 4 Fast and Devstral 2512 under the paraphrasing instruction of Park et al., 2025), the deterministic fold assignment, the 105-feature matrix, the cross-prompt corpus (the same 1,050 files rewritten under two further instructions), 2,400 human revisions of source files from MIT-licensed repositories (the negative set of the paired detection experiment), the out-of-fold outputs of every view and baseline (tree learners, TF-IDF views, fine-tuned CodeBERT and CodeT5 encoders, attention classifier, LPcodedec replication), every result file behind the article's tables and figures, the Colab notebooks for the GPU baselines, and the scripts that rebuild the corpus, run every experiment and regenerate every table and figure. The human-written files come from public repositories under the MIT, Apache 2.0, BSD 2-Clause and BSD 3-Clause licences and are redistributed under those licences with their notices preserved. Personal markers in identifiers were anonymised. The scripts are released under the MIT licence. The LPcode benchmark and the LPcodedec code of Park et al. are not redistributed; the README documents how to obtain them.
title: STACAD: replication package for 'Attributing paraphrased source code to the large language model that rewrote it'

summary: Iris biometric authentication systems employ the exclusive texture patterns of the iris to identify an individual; they can be very stable over time and are well suited for secure identity verification applications. Protecting stored iris templates is difficult, however, because of privacy concerns, irreversible exposure to iris biometrics and diminished authentication confidence if the templates are compromised. For iris recognition, researchers have developed new techniques based on deep learning to achieve better performance in feature extraction and classification. Frequently, however, these methods have weak template security, lack of feature optimization, and lack of scalability for authentication in cloud-based environments. Thus, researchers proposed the ACH-CIR: Attention-Guided Hybrid CNN–ANN Framework for Secure Cancelable Iris Recognition in Cloud Computing Environments. The pre-processing of iris images is done by segmentation, normalization and enhancement techniques in ACH-CIR model which is based on USIT framework. It then transforms the data using secure cancelable transformation through BLAKE3 hashing, generation of user-specific seed-matrix, and inverse feature transformation for privacy preservation. Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) are used to extract features and an attention mechanism is further used to optimize the features. The hybrid deep learning integration consists of extracting the features using CNN and authentication using ANNs for iris authentication. Such metrics as accuracy, precision, recall, GAR, FAR, FRR and EER are used to measure performance. The proposed Attention-guided CNN–ANN model is able to provide better recognition accuracy and protection for template in standard CASIA iris datasets. The method could lead to a substantial enhancement of secure biometric authentication, as it allows for accurate, revocable and scalable iris recognition in cloud computing environments.

summary: Replication package for the systematic literature review "Production-Oriented Evaluation and Testing of LLM-Based Agents: A Systematic Literature Review" (revised version, submitted to Information and Software Technology; first submitted as "Evaluation and Testing of LLM-Based Agents in Production: A Systematic Literature Review"). The review follows Kitchenham–Charters guidelines with PRISMA 2020 reporting. The main search covers Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore and the ACM Digital Library up to 24 March 2026; with citation tracking it yields a review corpus of 88 primary studies (74 from the main search, 14 from citation tracking). A search extension to 25 September 2026 with the same query and criteria yields 314 further studies, reported as a separate update analysis. A Scopus sensitivity search with broader production-oriented terms (300-record random sample) estimates the recall of the query. Version 2.0.0 accompanies the revised article. Version 1.0.0 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20583928) accompanies the article as first submitted and is preserved unchanged in the folder 2026-03/. Contents: corpus/, extraction/, risk-of-bias/ — the review corpus of 88: included and excluded studies with screening decisions, dual data extraction (Reviewer 1, Reviewer 2 and arbiter-resolved; 27 analytical fields) and three-domain quality assessment. 2026-03/ — the March 2026 round exactly as released in v1.0.0 (80 studies, agreement reports, audits). 2026-09/ — the September 2026 round: ACM Digital Library and update searches (full-text records R001–R670), Scopus sensitivity search, extraction and quality assessment of 335 studies, agreement reports, and the single-label recode of automated-testing with its held-out validation. primary-studies.bib (88) and 2026-09/primary-studies.bib (335). reproduce.ipynb — a self-contained notebook with 595 automated checks that reproduce every statistic of the article computed from the per-record data (Section 2: review corpus; Section 3: September round; Appendix A: the 2026-03 round as first submitted). README.md (structure, data dictionary, errata), CHANGELOG.md, methodology.md, statistical-analyses.md, prisma-2020-checklist.md, kitchenham-2007-compliance.md, requirements.txt, LICENSE. To reproduce: install the dependencies (pip install -r requirements.txt) and run reproduce.ipynb top to bottom. Expected output: 595 checks passed, 0 failed. Licensed under CC BY 4.0.
title: Replication package for "Production-Oriented Evaluation and Testing of LLM-Based Agents: A Systematic Literature Review"

Contents: the corpus of 144,958 paraphrase pairs (22,053 human-written files in Python, C, C++, Java, C#, Go and PHP, rewritten by Gemini 3 Flash, GPT 5 Nano, Claude 3 Haiku, Qwen 3 Coder 30B, DeepSeek V3.2, Grok 4 Fast and Devstral 2512 under the paraphrasing instruction of Park et al., 2025), the deterministic fold assignment, the 105-feature matrix, the cross-prompt corpus (the same 1,050 files rewritten under two further instructions), 2,400 human revisions of source files from MIT-licensed repositories (the negative set of the paired detection experiment), the out-of-fold outputs of every view and baseline (tree learners, TF-IDF views, fine-tuned CodeBERT and CodeT5 encoders, attention classifier, LPcodedec replication), every result file behind the article's tables and figures, the Colab notebooks for the GPU baselines, and the scripts that rebuild the corpus, run every experiment and regenerate every table and figure. The human-written files come from public repositories under the MIT, Apache 2.0, BSD 2-Clause and BSD 3-Clause licences and are redistributed under those licences with their notices preserved. Personal markers in identifiers were anonymised. The scripts are released under the MIT licence. The LPcode benchmark and the LPcodedec code of Park et al. are not redistributed; the README documents how to obtain them.
title: STACAD: replication package for 'Attributing paraphrased source code to the large language model that rewrote it'

summary: Derived data, code, frozen predictors and forward-test artifacts supporting the manuscript "Ambulance Station Siting under Extreme Heat: Coverage Equity in Phoenix and a Test of Decision-Focused Learning against Two-Stage Prediction" (Hong Yan). Version 1.2 adds: (i) the 2026 forward-window evaluation, with the analysis plan fixed on 2026-10-04 before the 2026 outcome data were downloaded, the evaluation script, daily results under both formulations, data provenance and a code-path reproduction check; (ii) a time-of-day congestion robustness layer built from the Maricopa Association of Governments 2026 Travel Demand Model, deposited as aggregated area-type and facility-type factors and derived coverage matrices only (no MAG link records); (iii) the survival-weighted coverage surrogate, its congested variant and the three-day stress test recomputed for the 2S-MSE allocation (the earlier files cover the SPO+ allocation); (iv) corrected documentation (solver: PuLP with CBC; travel times from the public OSRM routing server). A development log and a retired packaging script are removed. The forward commitments timestamped by version 1.1 (published 2026-06-01: frozen 2S-MSE pipeline, forward window 2026-06-02 to 2026-09-30, and the diagnostic prediction of an approximately 0.06 percentage-point 2S-MSE advantage at K/N = 0.679) are unchanged and are evaluated in this version. summary: This reproducibility package accompanies the article “Decomposing cross-study disagreement in renewable-energy priorities: a provenance-preserving typed RASS framework for Türkiye”. It contains the machine-readable source registry, source-extracted numerical tables with article-level provenance, typed records, configuration and policy files, Python analysis code, tests, computational certificates, derived outputs, and figure and table source assets supporting the reported analyses. The package supports source-native replication audits of four published Türkiye renewable-energy prioritization studies; controlled representation and operator experiments; ordinal and numerical evidence synthesis; weight–ontology–missingness robustness analyses; and theorem-certificate checks. Copyrighted publisher PDF files are not included. The source articles are identified through their bibliographic information and DOIs in the source registry. No personal or sensitive data are included. Version 1.0. Usage and reproduction instructions are provided in README.md, and file integrity information is provided in SHA256SUMS.txt.

summary: Ejikeme, P. O. (2026). The Obi Phenomenon and Political Agency in Nigeria: A Phenomenological Interpretation of Democratic Participation. Afrisophia: Journal of African Experiment, Thought and Experience, 3 (3), 123–136.     https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23131893   Abstract  This paper addresses a central problem in Nigerian democracy: why did the 2023 general elections generate an unprecedented youth-led mobilization that challenged the hegemony of entrenched party structures, ethno-regional politics and patronage, despite its failure to produce electoral victory? It poses the philosophical question: Can the "Obi Phenomenon" be understood not merely as an electoral contest around the personality of Peter Obi, but as an ethical demand for a moral and political reconfiguration of citizenship, accountability, and collective agency? This study is a qualitative political analysis using phenomenological interpretation. It adopts analytic and phenomenological tools of philosophy to interrogate the lived experience and meaning of youth political participation. The paper draws from African philosophical ideologies as its conceptual framework, particularly the principle of communality and complementarity in African philosophy - Igwebuike - theorized here as a philosophy of "we-ness", in dialogue with theories of participatory democracy and civic virtue. The analysis is grounded in the phenomenology of the 2023 electoral cycle, including patterns of youth voter registration and turnout, digital mobilization and political discourse on social media platforms, the public articulation of values of frugality, competence and inclusion and documented challenges to traditional clientelist expectations. The paper argues that the Obi Phenomenon represents a shift from clientelist to value-based politics in Nigeria. Its significance lies not in electoral outcome, but in institutionalizing a new grammar of political participation - one anchored on ethical leadership and collective agency - with enduring implications for democratic consolidation in Nigeria beyond 2027.   Keywords: Nigerian Politics, Obi Phenomenon, I gwebuike , Digital Democracy, Citizenship, Youth Mobilization, Obidient
title: The Obi Phenomenon and Political Agency in Nigeria: A Phenomenological Interpretation of Democratic Participation

summary: Supporting material for the manuscript "The Quantum Noise Fraction and the Addressable Fraction in High-Frequency Gravitational Wave Detection" by S. Gaudio (arXiv:2605.00053). This version updates and extends all numerical and data values of v3 of the paper. The record contains the three figures of the manuscript with their generating scripts; the Python scripts that recompute every numerical result (verify_all_results.py, 275 checks; an independently written cross-check, verify_independent.py;  a check of the Goryachev-Tobar expressions against their published erratum, check_GT_erratum.py); a workbook with live formulas (HF_beta_data.xlsx); and PROVENANCE_of_numbers.md, which states for every number whether it is recomputed, verified against the cited source with quotation, or our own declared reading or assumption. See README.md for the contents and the changes from version 2. Requires Python with numpy, scipy, matplotlib and openpyxl. Code: MIT License; data and documentation: CC BY 4.0 (see LICENSE).
